fields.name: COPY_IN_PROGRESS
fields.description: This field specifies that ADDDC sparing copy is on-going for this region. This bit should be set by BIOS before starting the ADDDC sparing copy flow. This bit should be cleared by hardware at the end of the sparing copy flow.

fields.name: NONFAILED_BG
fields.description: This field specifies the bank group to match when determining if this is the non- failed region participating in ADDDC. Only used when region_size=bank.

fields.name: NONFAILED_BA
fields.description: This field specifies the bank address to match when determining if this is the non-failed region participating in ADDDC. Only used when region_size=bank.

fields.name: NONFAILED_C
fields.description: This field specifies the 3DS subrank to match when determining if this is the non-failed region participating in ADDDC. Only used when region_size=bank.

fields.name: NONFAILED_CS
fields.description: This field specifies the rank to match when determining if this is the non-failed region participating in ADDDC mode. The rank value matches the format of the logged value as in retry_rd_err_log_address1.chip_select.

fields.name: FAILED_BG
fields.description: This field specifies the bank group to match when determining if this is the failed region participating in ADDDC. Only used when region_size=bank.

fields.name: FAILED_BA
fields.description: This field specifies the bank address to match when determining if this is the failed region participating in ADDDC. Only used when region_size=bank.

fields.name: FAILED_C
fields.description: This field specifies the 3DS subrank to match when determining if this is the failed region participating in ADDDC. Only used when region_size=bank.

fields.name: RSVD
fields.description: continued... Diamond Rapids Processor June 2026 Registers Specification Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 Intel Confidential 4587

fields.name: FAILDEVICE
fields.description: This field specifies the failed device to be mapped out for this adddc region. Valid range is 0-9, for failed device from sddc mode. ADDDC logic internally determines if the failed device is in primary or buddy rank.

fields.name: REGION_SIZE
fields.description: Granularity for this ADDDC region: 00=bank 01=rank 10=reserved 11=reserved

fields.name: REGION_ENABLE
fields.description: This bit specifies whether the ADDDC region is in use. 0=ADDDC not enabled for this region 1=ADDDC enabled for this region This bit should be set by software before the beginning of the ADDDC sparing copy flow. When any ADDDC region is enabled, writes from ADDDC region will be BC8, and BC8 on-the-fly (OTF) mode needs to be selected. Then any scheduler timing programming needs to obey BC8 requirements.

BIOS_HSFSTS_CTL.name: BIOS_HSFSTS_CTL

fields.name: FSMIE
fields.description: When set to 1, the SPI asserts an SMI# request whenever the Flash Cycle Done bit is 1.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: FDBC
fields.description: This field specifies the number of bytes to shift in or out during the data portion of the SPI cycle. The contents of this register are 0s based with 0b representing 1 byte and 3Fh representing 64 bytes. The number of bytes transferred is the value of this field plus 1. This field is ignored for the Block Erase command.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: WET
fields.description: • 0: Use 06h as the write enable instruction • 1: Use 50h as the write enable instruction Note: No supported flash devices require the 50h opcode to enable a non-volatile status register write. This bit is no longer required.

fields.name: FCYCLE
fields.description: RSecure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers-Diamond Rapids Processor 11879332 Guohui Y This field defines the Flash SPI cycle type generated to the FLASH when the FGO bit is set as defined below: • 0h: Read (1 up to 64 bytes by setting FDBC) • 1h: Reserved • 2h: Write (1 up to 64 bytes by setting FDBC) • 3h: 4k Block Erase • 4h: 64k Sector erase • 5h: Read SFDP • 6h: Read JEDEC ID • 7h: write status • 8h: read status • 9h: Reserved • Ah: Reserved • Bh: Reserved • Ch: Reserved • Dh: Reserved • Eh: Reserved • Fh: Reserved Flash controller hardware automatically inserts a write enable opcode prior to Write and erase operations. Write, Erase cycles are deterimined as Completed after device not-busy is cleared using read status operations. If the device does not support 64k erase size (or if it doesn't support SFDP) then only 4k is allowed. See Program Register Access section for opcode values. Note: if any reserved value is programmed to this field, flash controller will handle it as if it is 0 (Read).

fields.name: /1S/V
fields.description: FGO Field (FGO): A write to this register with a '1' in this bit initiates a request to the Flash SPI Arbiter to start a cycle. This register is cleared by hardware when the cycle is granted by the SPI arbiter to run the cycle on the SPI bus. When the cycle is complete, the FDONE bit is set. Software is forbidden to write to any register in the HSFLCTL register between the FGO bit getting set and the FDONE bit being cleared. Any attempt to violate this rule will be ignored by hardware. Hardware allows other bits in this register to be programmed for the same transaction when writing this bit to 1. This saves an additional memory write. This bit remains set until the transaction is granted by the SPI Controller's internal arbiter. Note: This bit always returns 0 on reads.

fields.name: FLOCKDN
fields.description: When set to 1, those Flash Program Registers that are locked down by this FLOCKDN bit cannot be written. Once set to 1, this bit can only be cleared by a hardware reset. Locked by: BIOS_HSFSTS_CTL

fields.name: FDV
fields.description: This bit is set to a 1 if the Flash Controller read the correct Flash Descriptor Signature. If the Flash Descriptor Valid bit is not 1, software cannot use the Hardware Sequencing registers, but must use the software sequencing registers. Any attempt to use the Hardware Sequencing registers will result in the FCERR bit being set.

fields.name: FDOPSS
fields.description: Read only as '1' which indicates No Flash Descriptor Override Strap

fields.name: PRR34_LOCKDN
fields.description: Since DLOCK register is implemented, this bit is not used to lock down the BIOS PRR3 and PRR4 registers. It becomes a dummy bit that locks itself. R Diamond Rapids Processor-Secure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers Registers Specification June 2026 1960 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 Note: Once set to 1, this bit can only be cleared by a hardware reset. Locked by: BIOS_HSFSTS_CTL

fields.name: WRSDIS
fields.description: • 0: Write status operation may be issued using Hardware Sequencing. • 1: Write status is not allowed as a Hardware Sequencing operation. The flash controller will block the operation and set the FCERR bit when software sets the 'go' bit. Locked by: BIOS_HSFSTS_CTL

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: H_SAF_CE
fields.description: Sets this bit to 1 when a transaction is returned from the eSPI controller with ctype error. See eSPI Error Status registers for additional details.

fields.name: H_SAF_MODE_ACTIVE
fields.description: • 0: indicates flash is attached directly via the SPI bus • 1: indicates flash is attached to the BMC and is accessed via tunneled eSPI flash channel commands. a.k.a eDAF mode.

fields.name: H_SAF_LE
fields.description: Sets this bit to 1 when a transaction is returned from the eSPI channel with link error.

fields.name: H_SCIP
fields.description: Hardware sets this bit when software sets the Flash Cycle Go (FGO) bit in the Hardware Sequencing Flash Control register. This bit remains set until the cycle completes on the SPI interface or the transaction is prevented due to any protection policy violation (descriptor, address range, protected region, etc). Hardware automatically sets and clears this bit so that software can determine when read data is valid and/or when it is safe to begin programming the next command. Software must only program the next command when this bit is 0. Note: Software shall not trigger a new SPI Cycle while SCIP is asserted, otherwise, it may cause un-defined behavior.

fields.name: H_SAF_DLE
fields.description: sets this bit to 1 when a transaction is returned from the eSPI flash channel with an incorrect data length.

fields.name: H_SAF_ERROR
fields.description: sets this bit to 1 when a transaction is requested that is not supported by eSPI Device-Attached flash, e.g. read status.

fields.name: H_AEL
fields.description: Hardware sets this bit to a 1 when an attempt was made to access the BIOS region using the direct access method or an access to the BIOS Program Registers that violated the security restrictions. This bit is simply a log of an access security violation. Note: This bit is cleared by software writing a '1'.

fields.name: FCERR
fields.description: Hardware sets this bit to 1 when a program register access is blocked to the FLASH due to one of the protection policies or when any of the programmed cycle registers is written while a programmed access is already in progress. Note: This bit remains asserted until cleared by software writing a 1 or until hardware reset occurs. Note: Software must clear this bit before setting the FLASH Cycle GO bit in this register.

fields.name: FDONE
fields.description: RSecure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers-Diamond Rapids Processor The SPI Controller sets this bit to 1 when the SPI Cycle completes after software previously set the FGO bit. This bit remains asserted until cleared by software writing a 1 or hardware reset. When this bit is set and the SPI SMI# Enable bit is set, an internal signal is asserted to the SMI# generation block. Software must make sure this bit is cleared prior to enabling the SPI SMI# assertion for a new programmed access.

fields.name: MEMBAR
fields.description: Software programs this register with the base address of the device's memory region. The Host/BIOS MMIO registers in the flash controller are offset from this BAR.

fields.description: Hardwired to 0 to indicate 4KB of memory space.

fields.name: PREFETCH

fields.description: Hardwired to 0 to indicate that Base register is 32 bits wide and mapping can be done anywhere in the 32-bit Memory Space.

fields.description: Hardwired to 0 to identify a Memory BAR.

fields.name: /P
fields.description: Viral Status (VSTS): When set, indicates that the Upstream Switch Port or the Downstream Switch Port has entered Viral. See (see Section 12.4 for more details). This bit is not applicable to Root ports, and reads shall return the value of 0.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: PWMIC
fields.description: When set, it indicates that the root port, the Upstream Switch Port or the Downstream Switch Port has successfully completed the Power Management Initialization Flow as described in Figure 3-4 and is ready to process various Power Management events. If this bit is not set within 100 ms of link-up, software may conclude that the Power Management initialization has failed and may issue Secondary Bus Reset to force link re-initialization and Power Management re-initialization. Port specific may not be valid and is pending on bifurcation and CXL min. width (X4) supported if applicable. -V with dependency on C2PTESTSS.PWMIC and cleared by HW when the CXL_DEVICE_CHANGE.ADD = 0 IOSF-SB message is sent.

sections: Completer Abort Error Conditions CMD_STAT_REG CMD_STAT_REG CMD_STAT_REG

fields.name: STATUS_SIGNALED_SYSTEM_ERROR
fields.description: (STATUS_SIGNALED_SYSTEM_ERROR): This bit is set when the device has detected an un-correctable error and reported it via SERR message over sideband. This requires SERR Enable bit to be set in Command register.

fields.name: STATUS_SIGNALED_TARGET_ABORT
fields.description: (STATUS_SIGNALED_TARGET_ABORT): Set by the device when aborting a request that violates the device programming model. When SERR Enable is set SERR message will be send over sideband.

fields.name: STATUS_NEW_CAP
fields.description: Indicates that a device implements extended capabilities. The Controller sets this bit, and implements a capabilities list.

fields.name: STATUS_INTERRUPT_STATUS
fields.description: The Interrupt Status field is a RO field that indicates that an interrupt message is pending internally to the device.

fields.name: COMMAND_INTERRUPT_DISABLE
fields.description: (COMMAND_INTERRUPT_DISABLE): Controls the ability of a device to generate a legacy interrupt message. When set, the device cannot generate legacy interrupt messages.

fields.name: COMMAND_SERR_ENABLE
fields.description: 1=Enable SERR# Generation

fields.name: COMMAND_BUS_ACCESS_ENABLE
fields.description: (COMMAND_BUS_ACCESS_ENABLE): Must be set to 1 for the device to initiate memory read and write requests as a Driver/Initiator. This bit does not affect a device's ability to generate MSI message, Error Message, or completion cycles as a target.

fields.name: COMMAND_MEM_ACCESS_ENABLE
fields.description: (COMMAND_MEM_ACCESS_ENABLE): When set, Memory Space Decoding is enabled and Memory transactions targeting the device are accepted

fields.name: COMMAND_IO_ACCESS_ENABLE
fields.description: (COMMAND_IO_ACCESS_ENABLE): When set, IO Space Decoding is enabled and IO transactions targeting the device are accepted

CORERRTH.name: CORERRTH

fields.name: ERRTH
fields.description: Link correctable error threshold. Non zero threshold value enables the correctable error counter. When the Correctable Error Counter is enabled, an internal ERR_COR message is generated when the counter becomes equal to threshold. If threshold is 15 and count is 14, the next correctable error generates 1 Correctable error message. Same holds true for count and threshold of 0xFFFFFFFF. CORERRCNT.ERRCNT would be saturated, i.e. stops counting at 0xFFFFFFFF accordingly.

fields.name: REGION_ENABLE
fields.description: This bit specifies whether the ADDDC region is in use. 0=ADDDC not enabled for this region 1=ADDDC enabled for this region This bit should be set by software before the beginning of the ADDDC sparing copy flow. DL_Active ERR_COR Enable (DLAECE):
This bit must be RW if the DL_Active ERR_COR Signaling Supported bit is Set,
otherwise, it is permitted to be hardwired to 0b. Software must not Set this bit
unless the DL_Active ERR_COR Signaling Supported bit is Set.
When Set, this bit enables the associated Downstream Port to signal with
ERR_COR when the Link transitions to the DL_Active state.
6 0h
RW/V
DPC Software Trigger (DPCST):
This bit must be RW if the DPC Software Triggering Supported bit is Set,
otherwise, it is permitted to be hardwired to 0b.
If DPC is enabled and the DPC Trigger Status bit is Clear, when software writes
1b to this bit, DPC is triggered. Otherwise, software writing a 1b to this bit has
no effect.
It is permitted to write 1b to this bit while simultaneously writing updated values
to other fields in this register, notably the DPC Trigger Enable field. For this case,
the DPC Software Trigger semantics are based on the updated value of the DPC
Trigger Enable field.
This bit always returns 0b when read.
5 0h
RW/V
Poisoned TLP Egress Blocking Enable (PTLPEBE):
This bit must be RW if the Poisoned TLP Egress Blocking Supported bit is Set,
otherwise, it is permitted to be hardwired to 0b. Software must not Set this bit
unless the Poisoned TLP Egress Blocking Supported bit is Set.
When Set, this bit enables the associated Egress Port to block the transmission
of poisoned TLPs.
4 0h
RW/V
DPC ERR_COR Enable (DPCECE):
When Set, this bit enables the sending of an ERR_COR Message to indicate that
DPC has been triggered.

ECC_CORR_BIST.name: ECC_CORR_BIST
sections: Correctable error (UC=0, PCC=0) for data UC errors corrected by FM fill.
bist_en 1'b1 RW This bit is used to enable PFD in the ECC correction path.

fields.name: BIST_CORR_MODE
fields.description: When set to 1, PFD is used to correct single device DUE case. If this bit is set to 1, bist_err_report_mode bit should be programmed to 0.

fields.name: BIST_CE_CORRFSM_NOERR
fields.description: This bit is used to program the final result for the case when PFD gives CE and correction fsm gives NoErorr. Values it can take are: 00 -> UC 01 -> CE 10 -> NoError (Recommended)

fields.name: BIST_ERR_REPORT_MODE
fields.description: This bit is used to select PFD to work in Error Reporting Mode. In this mode, only PFD results are logged, but they are not considered to make the final decision in the ECC correction path.

fields.name: BIST_EN

ERRUNCMSK.name: ERRUNCMSK
ERRUNCMSK.eds_description: This register controls the reporting of individual uncorrectable errors by device to the host bridge via a PCI Express error message. This register also controls the logging of the header. Refer to the PCI Express specifications for details of how the mask bits function. A masked error (respective bit set in the mask register) is not reported to the host bridge by the switch, nor is the header logged (status bits unaffected by the mask bit). There is a mask bit per bit of the Uncorrectable Error Status Register. The attr. of AER Error Mask bits in VRSP will be changed to be compliant with PCIe Spec.

ERROR COUNTER CONTROL (ERR_CNTR_CTL) - Offset 2D4h
Saturating error counters (6b) in the bridge, track the number of transactions which
had a memory controller error. A transaction in this context is an SMI3 transaction
from the mesh (NOT commands to iMC). So even if multiple retries are sent to the
memory controller, the retried commands to the iMC are not counted individually.
This control register allows indirect access to these bridge txn error counters; Reading
the counters of a particular error type, or clearing all the counters.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: SAFCAMEMPTY
fields.description: Only valid in device-attached flash mode. Will always read 1 otherwise. • 0: SAF CAM is not empty - there are outstanding NP flash transactions to the eSPI device. • 1: SAF CAM is empty - there are no outstanding NP flash transactions to the eSPI device. Reset Source: Register bit is reset on IA warm reset R Diamond Rapids Processor-Secure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers Registers Specification June 2026 1702 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15

fields.name: SAFBLK
fields.description: Only valid in device-attached flash mode. Will never be set to 1 by hardware otherwise. Set to 1 by hardware, when SAF NF Error Blocking Enable is set, when a NON_FATAL_ERROR response is received in response to a GET_FLASH_C. When this bit is set, the eSPI Driver/Initiator will not issue any additional transactions on the flash channel. Software must write a 1 to clear this bit. Reset Source: Register bit is reset on IA warm reset

fields.name: SAFNFEBLKEN
fields.description: Only valid in device-attached flash mode. Has no impact otherwise. • 1: the flash channel will be blocked when a NON_FATAL_ERROR response is received in response to a GET_FLASH_C. • 0: the flash channel will NOT be blocked when a NON_FATAL_ERROR response is received in response to a GET_FLASH_C. Reset Source: Register bit is reset on IA warm reset

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: FCNFEE
fields.description: • 00: Disable Non-Fatal Error Reporting • 01: Reserved • 10: Enable Non-Fatal Error Reporting as SERR (SB Do_SErr message) • 11: Enable Non-Fatal Error Reporting as SMI (Assert_SMI from eSPI service to SMI service) Note: SERR enable is also qualified by PCCMD.SEE (Offset 04h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. Note: SERR also sets PCSTS.SSE (Offset 06h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. Note: SMI/SERR messages are not generated if the Host is in reset (PLTRST# asserted). Reset Source: Register bit is reset on IA warm reset

fields.name: FCNFES
fields.description: This field is set by hardware if a Non-Fatal Error condition is detected on the Flash Access Channel. Software must clear this bit. • 0: No Non-Fatal Error detected • 1: Non-Fatal Error detected (FCNFEC has a non-zero value) Note: Clearing this unlocks and sets to default value the FCNFEC field and triggers an IOSF-SB Deassert_SMI message if FCNFEE is set to SMI. Note: Setting of this bit is independent of the enable to generate a SMI/SERR (FCNFEE). Reset Source: Register bit is reset on IA warm reset

fields.name: FCNFEC
fields.description: 0h: No error 1h: eSPI-Device Response Code: NONFATAL_ERROR in response to GET_FLASH_NP, GET_FLASH_C 2h: eSPI-Device Cycle Type: Unsuccessful Completion Unsuccessful Completion [for eSPI-Device-Attached Flash accesses only] 3h: Unexpected completion received from eSPI-Device (i.e. completion without non-posted request or completion with invalid tag or completion with invalid length) (for eSPI-Device Attached Flash accesses only) 5h: Reserved 7h: Reserved 8h - Fh: Reserved Note: This field is updated to default value by clearing (1C) of FCNFES. RSecure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers-Diamond Rapids Processor Reset Source: Register bit is reset on IA warm reset

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: FCFEE
fields.description: • 00: Disable Fatal Error Reporting • 01: Reserved • 10: Enable Fatal Error Reporting as SERR (SB Do_SErr message) • 11: Enable Fatal Error Reporting as SMI (Assert_SMI from eSPI service to SMI service) Note: SERR enable is also qualified by PCCMD.SEE (Offset 04h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. Note: SERR also sets PCSTS.SSE (Offset 06h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. Note: SMI/SERR messages are not generated if the Host is in reset (PLTRST# asserted). Reset Source: Register bit is reset on IA cold reset Note: This is reserved on S3M IBL as scratchpad with no function since FCFES is always Read Only as 1'b0.

fields.name: FCFES
fields.description: This field is set by hardware if a Fatal Error condition is detected on the Flash Access Channel. Software must clear this bit by writing a 1 to it. • 0: No Fatal Error detected • 1: Fatal Error (Type 1) detected (FCFEC has a non-zero value) Note: Clearing this unlocks and sets to default the FCFEC field and triggers an IOSF-SB Deassert_SMI message if FCFEE is set to SMI. Note: Setting of this bit is independent of the enable to generate a SMI/SERR (FCFEE). Reset Source: Register bit is reset on IA cold reset Note: This is reserved on S3M IBL as there is no separate Fatal Error Cause that will set FCFES.

fields.name: FCFEC
fields.description: • 0h: No error • 1h - 7h: Reserved • Ah - Fh: Reserved Reset Source: Register bit is reset on IA cold reset

HCTL.name: HCTL
sections: When set, this indicates that the source of the interrupt or 1 Set bit 0

fields.name: PEC_EN
fields.description: When set to 1, this bit causes the host controller to perform the SMBus transaction with the Packet Error Checking phase appended. For writes, the value of the PEC byte is transferred from the PEC Register. For reads, the PEC byte is loaded in to the PEC Register. When this bit is cleared to 0, the SMBus host controller does not perform the transaction with the PEC phase appended. This bit must be written prior to the write in which the START bit is set.

fields.name: START
fields.description: This write-only bit is used to initiate the command described in the SMB_CMD field. All registers should be setup prior to writing a 1 to this bit position. This bit always reads zero. The HOST_BUSY bit in the Host Status register (offset 00h) can be used to identify when the controller has finished the command.

fields.name: LAST_BYTE
fields.description: Used for I2C Read commands as an indication that the next byte will be the last one to be received for that block. The algorithm and usage model for this bit will be as follows (assume a message of n bytes): • A. When the software sees the BYTE_DONE_STS bit set (bit 7 in the SMBus Host Status Register) for each of bytes 1 through n-2 of the message, the software should then read the Block Data Byte Register to get the byte that was just received. • B. After reading each of bytes 1 to n-2 of the message, the software will then clear the BYTE_DONE_STS bit. • C. After receiving byte n-1 of the message, the software will then set the LAST BYTE bit. The software will then clear the BYTE_DONE_STS bit. • D. The SMBus Host Controller will then receive the last byte of the message (byte n). However, the SMBus Host Controller state machine will see the LAST BYTE bit set, and instead of sending an ACK after receiving the last byte, it will instead send a NAK. • E. After receiving the last byte (byte n), the software will still clear the BYTE_DONE_STS bit. However, the LAST_BYTE bit will be irrelevant at that point. Note: This bit may be set when the TCO timer causes the SECOND_TO_STS bit to be set. See the TCO2_STS Register in Volume 1, bit 1 for more details on that bit. The SMBus device driver should clear the LAST_BYTE bit (if it is set) before starting any new command. Note: In addition to I2C Read Commands, the LAST_BYTE bit will also cause Block Read/Write cycles to stop prematurely (at the end of the next byte).

fields.name: SMB_CMD
fields.description: As shown by the bit encoding below, indicates which command the SMBus Host Controller is to perform. If enabled, the SMBus Host Controller will generate an interrupt or SMI# when the command has completed If the value is for a non- supported or reserved command, the SMBus Host Controller will set the device error (DEV_ERR) status bit and generate an interrupt when the START bit is set. The SMBus Host Controller will perform no command, and will not operate until DEV_ERR is cleared. Val - Command Description: • 000 - Quick: The responder/target address and read/write value (bit 0) are stored in the tx responder/target address register. • 001 - Byte: This command uses the transmit responder/target address and command registers. Bit 0 of the responder/target address register determines if this is a read or write command. RSecure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers-Diamond Rapids Processor • 010 - Byte Data: This command uses the transmit responder/target address, command, and DATA0 registers. Bit 0 of the responder/target address register determines if this is a read or write command. If it is a read, the DATA0 register will contain the read data. • 011 - Word Data: This command uses the transmit responder/target address, command, DATA0 and DATA1 registers. Bit 0 of the responder/target address register determines if this is a read or write command. If it is a read, after the command completes the DATA0 and DATA1 registers will contain the read data. • 100 - Process Call: This command uses the transmit responder/target address, command, DATA0 and DATA1 registers. Bit 0 of the responder/target address register determines if this is a read or write command. After the command completes, the DATA0 and DATA1 registers will contain the read data. • 101 - Block: This command uses the transmit responder/target address,command, and DATA0 registers, and the Block Data Byte register. For block write, the count is stored in the DATA0 register and indicates how many bytes of data will be transferred. For block reads, the count is received and stored in the DATA0 register. Bit 0 of the responder/target address register selects if this is a read or write command. For writes, data is retrieved from the first n (where n is equal to the specified count) addresses of the SRAM array. For reads, the data is stored in the Block Data Byte register. • 110 - I2C Read: This command uses the transmit responder/target address, command, DATA0, DATA1 registers, and the Block Data Byte register. The read data is stored in the Block Data Byte register. The SMBus Host Controller will continue reading data until the NAK is received. • 111 - Block-Process: This command uses the transmit responder/target address, command, DATA0 and the Block Data Byte register. For block write, the count is stored in the DATA0 register and indicates how many bytes of data will be transferred. For block read, the count is received and stored in the DATA0 register. Bit 0 of the responder/target address register always indicate a write command. For writes, data is retrieved from the first m (where m is equal to the specified count) addresses of the SRAM array. For reads, the data is stored in the Block Data Byte register. Note: E32B bit in the Auxiliary Control Register must be set for this command to work.

fields.name: KILL
fields.description: When set, kills the current host transaction taking place, sets the FAILED status bit, and asserts the interrupt (or SMI#) selected by the SMB_INTRSEL field. This bit, once set, must be cleared to allow the SMB Host Controller to function normally.

fields.name: INTREN
fields.description: Enable the generation of an interrupt or SMI# upon the completion of the command.

fields.name: BDS
fields.description: This bit will be set to 1 when the host controller has received a byte (for Block Read commands) or if it has completed transmission of a byte (for Block Write commands) when the 32-byte buffer is not being used. Note that this bit will be set, even on the last byte of the transfer. Software clears the bit by writing a 1 to the bit position.This bit has no meaning for block transfers when the 32- byte buffer is enabled. Note: When the last byte of a block message is received, the host controller will set this bit. However, it will not immediately set the INTR bit (bit 1 in this register). Diamond Rapids Processor June 2026 Registers Specification Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 Intel Confidential 1931

fields.name: IUS
fields.description: After a full PCI reset, a read to this bit returns a 0. After the first read, subsequent reads will return a 1. A write of a 1 to this bit will reset the next read value to 0. Writing a 0 to this bit has no effect. Software can poll this bit until it reads a 0, and will then own the usage of the host controller. This bit has no other effect on the hardware, and is only used as semaphore among various independent software threads that may need to use the SMBus logic.

fields.name: SMSTS
fields.description: SMBus Host Controller sets this bit to a 1 to indicates source of the interrupt or SMI# was the SMBAlert# signal. Software resets this bit by writing a 1 to this location. This bit should also be cleared by AUXPWRGOOD (but not PLTRST#).

fields.name: FAIL
fields.description: When set, this indicates that the source of the interrupt or SMI# was a failed bus transaction. This is set in response to the KILL bit being set to terminate the host transaction.

fields.name: BERR
fields.description: When set, this indicates the source of the interrupt or SMI# was a transaction collision.

fields.name: DERR
fields.description: When set, this indicates that the source of the interrupt or SMI# was due one of the following: Illegal Command Field Unclaimed Cycle (host initiated) Host Device Time-out Error. CRC Error

fields.name: INTR
fields.description: When set, this indicates that the source of the interrupt or SMI# was the successful completion of its last command.

fields.name: HBSY
fields.description: A 1 indicates that the SMBus Host Controller is running a command from the host interface. No SMB registers should be accessed while this bit is set. Exception: The BLOCK DATA REGISTER can be accessed when this bit is set ONLY when the SMB_CMD bits (in Host control register) are programmed for Block command or I2C Read command. This is necessary in order to check the DONE_STS bit.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Selects the threshold at which the corrected error count logged in the status register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to the CMCI LVT entry in the APIC when the count value equals the threshold value. The new LVT entry in the APIC is at 02F0H offset from the APIC_BASE. If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this field will always read 0.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW

able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition

IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW

Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW

where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the

address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.

Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: CMCI_EN
fields.description: Software sets this bit to enable the generation of corrected machine-check error interrupt (CMCI). If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this bit is writeable but will always return 0 for that bank. fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Selects the threshold at which the corrected error count logged in the status register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to the CMCI LVT entry in the APIC when the count value equals the threshold value. The new LVT entry in the APIC is at 02F0H offset from the APIC_BASE. If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this field will always read 0.

IA32_MC10_MISC.name: IA32_MC10_MISC

fields.name: MODEL_SPECIFIC_INFORMATION
fields.description: For IA32_MC4_STATUS.MCACOD = 0E0Bh: • [30:23] Contains the PCI segment number • [22:7] Contains the PCI requestor ID where: [22:15] Bus log [14:10] Device log [9:7] Function log For IA32_MC4_STATUS.MCACOD = 0412h: • [15:0] Contains port ID from IP generating an MCE. Refer to Error Logging Registers Decoding section for details.

fields.name: ADDRESS_MODE
fields.description: Address mode for the address logged in IA32_MCi_ADDR. The supported address modes are: Segment Offset(000), Linear Address(001), Physical Address(010), Memory Address(011), Generic(111), Reserved(100 to 110)

fields.name: RECOVERABLE_ADDRESS_LSB
fields.description: The lowest valid recoverable address bit. Indicates the position of the least significant bit of the recoverable error address. For example, if the processor logs bits [43:9] of the address, the LSB sub-field is 0b01001 (9 decimal). For this example, bits [8:0] of the recoverable error address in IA32_MCi_ADDR should be ignored.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.

Field Name (ID): Description
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

implemented in the processor.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.

fields.name: CMCI_EN
fields.description: Software sets this bit to enable the generation of corrected machine-check error interrupt (CMCI). fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Selects the threshold at which the corrected error count logged in the status register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to the CMCI LVT entry in the APIC when the count value equals the threshold value. The new LVT entry in the APIC is at 02F0H offset from the APIC_BASE. If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this field will always read 0.

IA32_MC11_MISC.name: IA32_MC11_MISC

fields.name: MODEL_SPECIFIC_INFORMATION
fields.description: • 1 - Indicates Pcode WathDog Timer expired. • 3 - Indicates Power Management Unit TeleSRAM double--bit ECC error detected.

fields.name: ADDRESS_MODE
fields.description: Address mode for the address logged in IA32_MCi_ADDR. The supported address modes are: Segment Offset(000), Linear Address(001), Physical Address(010), Memory Address(011), Generic(111), Reserved(100 to 110)

fields.name: RECOVERABLE_ADDRESS_LSB
fields.description: The lowest valid recoverable address bit. Indicates the position of the least significant bit of the recoverable error address. For example, if the processor logs bits [43:9] of the address, the LSB sub-field is 0b01001 (9 decimal). For this example, bits [8:0] of the recoverable error address in IA32_MCi_ADDR should be ignored.

IA32_MC11_STATUS.name: IA32_MC11_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.
57 0h
RW

Type Size Scope Offset Default MSR 64 bit MCA Domain 433h 000000000000000 0h Register Level Access: Read Access Write Access R W, OOB Bit Range Default and Access Field Name (ID): Description 63:9 00000000000 000h RW MODEL_SPECIFIC_INFORMATION: [55] MIRRORFAILOVER = An error occured on a memory channel of the mirror channel pair. The error was corrected by channel failover under mirroring. This implies an uncorrectable (i.e. no correctable by mirror scrub) error on a channel. After failover, the complete (failed) channel is no longer available as a mirror back-up. Exception: For UC on original read data return this field is zero. As the error is trigger before scrubbing poison and reading. [54]MIRRORCORRERR = Error was corrected during mirroring and primary channel scrubbed successfully.A successful mirror scrub implies an error on the primary channel got

corrected by reading the data from the secondary, writing that data to the primary channel and successfully reading back the data from the primary channel.Exception:For UC on original read data return this field is zero. As the error is trigger before scrubbing poison and reading. [53] MCCDMIRRFO = MC command was to an already permanently failed over channel/region (MirrFo) [52] MCCMDMIRRSEC = Error on secondary mirror channel (McCmdMirrSec). [51] MCCMDMIRRREGION = MC command was to a mirror region (McCmdMirrRegion) which might or might not have failed over (see McCmdMirrFo bit). [47] MCCMDVLD = Memory controller valid command got logged. If set, indicates an McCmd logged and can interpret McCmd fields. [46:43] MEMREGION = Indicates region type. If no bits are set, the memory region of the request is 1LM DDR or N/A for errors that do not report to these bits. [42:34] REQNODEID = Node ID of the requestor. Note that due to the HSF IACA NID Virtualization feature, this is a virtualized NID for IACA NIDs. It is still a physical NID for IOCA NIDs. In order to translate from a virtual to a physical NID, SW must do the reverse mapping of what's documented in hsf_iaca_nid_virt. [33:26] BANKINDEX = Index of HAMVF MCA bank. [25:20] REQOPCODE = This logs the opcode of the original request to HAMVF that generated the error. [19:12] TRKID = Unified Tracker Identifier. [11:2] ERRORTYPE = Depending on the type of error (as indicated by the info logged in MCi_STATUS),this field will log various attributes of the error. For a given error type, each bit isinterpreted as follows: For Read ECC errors bits • [11:10] Reserved • [9:7] Always set to 0. • [6] Scrub check rd returned uncorrected data (ECC correction is enabled during scrub check rd); - only applicable to MirrCorrErr and MirrFailover errors • [5] Scrub check rd returned good data (note that ECC correction is enabled during scrub check rd); - only applicable to MirrCorrErr and MirrFailover errors • [4] Txn could not be corrected by ECC; • [3] Txn had an ECC corrected error (corrected by ECC during retry) • [2] Txn had a transient error (corrected by retry without ECC) 8:6 0h RW ADDRESS_MODE: Address mode for the address logged in IA32_MCi_ADDR. The supported address modes are: Segment Offset(000), Linear Address(001), Physical Address(010), Memory Address(011), Generic(111), Reserved(100 to 110) 5:0 00h RW RECOVERABLE_ADDRESS_LSB: The lowest valid recoverable address bit. Indicates the position of the least significant bit of the recoverable error address. For example, if the processor logs bits [43:9] of the address, the LSB sub-field is 0b01001 (9 decimal). For this example, bits [8:0] of the recoverable error address in IA32_MCi_ADDR should be ignored. (434h) IA32_MC13_CTL Machine Check Control Register Enumerated by MSR.IA32_MCG_CAP.COUNT > 13. Type Size Scope Offset Default MSR 64 bit MCA Domain 431h 000000000000000 0h Register Level Access: Read Access Write Access R W, OOB Bit Range Default and Access Field Name (ID): Description 63 0h RW VALID: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it. 62 0h RW OVERFLOW: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred 61 0h RW UC: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition 60 0h RW EN: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register. continued... 30.3.328 R Diamond Rapids Processor-Model Specific Registers (MSRs) Diamond Rapids Processor Registers Specification June 2026 5600 Intel Confidential Doc. fields.name: CMCI_EN
fields.description: Software sets this bit to enable the generation of corrected machine-check error interrupt (CMCI). If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this bit is writeable but will always return 0 for that bank. This bit also indicates CMCI is supported or not supported in the corresponding bank.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Selects the threshold at which the corrected error count logged in the status register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to the CMCI LVT entry in the APIC when the count value equals the threshold value. The new LVT entry in the APIC is at 02F0H offset from the APIC_BASE. If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this field will always read 0.

fields.name: MODEL_SPECIFIC_INFORMATION
fields.description:
[55] MIRRORFAILOVER = An error occured on a memory channel of the mirror channel pair. The error was corrected by channel failover under mirroring. This implies an uncorrectable (i.e. no correctable by mirror scrub) error on a channel. After failover, the complete (failed) channel is no longer available as a mirror back-up. Exception: For UC on original read data return this field is zero. As the error is trigger before scrubbing poison and reading. [54]MIRRORCORRERR = Error was corrected during mirroring and primary channel scrubbed successfully.A successful mirror scrub implies an error on the primary channel got

corrected by reading the data from the secondary, writing that data to the primary channel and successfully reading back the data from the primary channel.Exception:For UC on original read data return this field is zero. As the error is trigger before scrubbing poison and reading. [53] MCCDMIRRFO = MC command was to an already permanently failed over channel/region (MirrFo) [52] MCCMDMIRRSEC = Error on secondary mirror channel (McCmdMirrSec). [51] MCCMDMIRRREGION = MC command was to a mirror region (McCmdMirrRegion) which might or might not have failed over (see McCmdMirrFo bit). [47] MCCMDVLD = Memory controller valid command got logged. If set, indicates an McCmd logged and can interpret McCmd fields. [46:43] MEMREGION = Indicates region type. Decoding: R Diamond Rapids Processor-Model Specific Registers (MSRs) Registers Specification June 2026 5602 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 Yu • 0 = 1LM CXL HDM-H. • 1 = 1LM CXL HDM-B. • 2 = 1LM HDM-DB. • 3 = Flat2LM. If no bits are set, the memory region of the request is 1LM DDR or N/A for errors that do not report to these bits. [42:34] REQNODEID = Node ID of the requestor. Note that due to the HSF IACA NID Virtualization feature, this is a virtualized NID for IACA NIDs. It is still a physical NID for IOCA NIDs. IA32_MC12_STATUS.name: IA32_MC12_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register. R Diamond Rapids Processor-Model Specific Registers (MSRs) Registers Specification June 2026 5600 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 ohui.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

fields.name: S
fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: AR
fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: THRESHOLD_BASED_STATUS
fields.description: Threshold-based error status

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit

fields.name: FW
fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator

fields.name: OTHER_INFO
fields.description: Machine Specific Architecture Error Code

fields.name: MSCOD
fields.description: Machine Check Model Specific Error Code

fields.name: MCACOD
fields.description: Machine Check Architecture Error Code

Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

processor was able to correct the error condition

Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h

OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h

Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition

IA32_MC13_STATUS.name: IA32_MC13_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

fields.name: S
fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: AR
fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: THRESHOLD_BASED_STATUS
fields.description: Threshold-based error status

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit

fields.name: FW
fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator

fields.name: OTHER_INFO
fields.description: Machine Specific Architecture Error Code

fields.name: MSCOD
fields.description: Machine Check Model Specific Error Code

fields.name: MCACOD
fields.description: Machine Check Architecture Error Code

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.

Field Name (ID): Description
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.
57 0h
RW
PCC:
Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the
processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that
reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag
indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be
able to restart

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.
