IA32_MC14_STATUS.name: IA32_MC14_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: R Diamond Rapids Processor-Model Specific Registers (MSRs) Registers Specification June 2026 5608 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

fields.name: S
fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: AR
fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: THRESHOLD_BASED_STATUS
fields.description: Threshold-based error status

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit

fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator

fields.description: Machine Specific Architecture Error Code

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.

IA32_MC15_STATUS.name: IA32_MC15_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: R Diamond Rapids Processor-Model Specific Registers (MSRs) Registers Specification June 2026 5612 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

fields.name: S
fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: AR
fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: THRESHOLD_BASED_STATUS
fields.description: Threshold-based error status

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit

fields.name: FW
fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator

fields.name: OTHER_INFO
fields.description: Machine Specific Architecture Error Code

fields.name: MSCOD
fields.description: Machine Check Model Specific Error Code

fields.name: MCACOD
fields.description: Machine Check Architecture Error Code

register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with
IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to

Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

IA32_MC16_STATUS.name: IA32_MC16_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register. hui.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

fields.name: S
fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: AR
fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: THRESHOLD_BASED_STATUS
fields.description: Threshold-based error status

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit

fields.name: FW
fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator

fields.name: OTHER_INFO
fields.description: Machine Specific Architecture Error Code

fields.name: MSCOD
fields.description: Machine Check Model Specific Error Code

fields.name: MCACOD
fields.description: Machine Check Architecture Error Code

Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: R Diamond Rapids Processor-Model Specific Registers (MSRs) Registers Specification June 2026 5618 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 guo Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.

MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

For WDB parity or ECC error, following bits are valid: [7:0]: this field indicates the WDB ID For DDR ECC errors, following bits are valid: [54]: Indicates if the error was transient error; transient error is indicated for demand reads, underfill reads for partial writes, patrol and sparing reads. [52:49]: ECC mode (not valid if Bit[54] = 1) • 0001 => SDDC 128b 1LM • 0010 = SDDC 125b 1LM • 0011 = SDDC 125b 2LM • 0100 = ADDDC 80b 1LM • 0101 = ADDDC 80b 2LM • 1001 = 5x8 128b 1LM • 1010 = 5x8 125b 1LM • 1011 = 5x8 125b 2LM • b0000 = = Invalid ECC Mode [47:46]: Rank in the format as defined in RETRY_RD_ERR_lOG_ADDRESS1.CHIP_SELECT. [45:42]: CBit, with bit 45 as spare to accommodate possible future growth in size. Logged value: {1'b0,sub_rank[2:0]} [40]: In DDR mode, Sub-channel ID [39:35]: Failed device number (not valid if Bit[54] = 1 or bit[33] = 0). For non- ADDDC the device number is between 0-9. for ADDDC device number between 0-8 and 10-19 (9 is the spare device) [34]: Failed x8 half device valid (not valid if Bit[54] = 1 or bit[33] = 0): Set to 1 if failure identified is in one half device only for 5x8 DIMM. fields.name: ADDRESS_MODE
fields.description: Address mode for the address logged in IA32_MCi_ADDR. The supported address modes are: Segment Offset(000), Linear Address(001), Physical Address(010), Memory Address(011), Generic(111), Reserved(100 to 110)

fields.name: RECOVERABLE_ADDRESS_LSB
fields.description: The lowest valid recoverable address bit. Indicates the position of the least significant bit of the recoverable error address. For example, if the processor logs bits [43:9] of the address, the LSB sub-field is 0b01001 (9 decimal). For this example, bits [8:0] of the recoverable error address in IA32_MCi_ADDR should be ignored.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h

OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.

fields.name: CMCI_EN
fields.description: Software sets this bit to enable the generation of corrected machine-check error interrupt (CMCI). fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Selects the threshold at which the corrected error count logged in the status register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to the CMCI LVT entry in the APIC when the count value equals the threshold value. The new LVT entry in the APIC is at 02F0H offset from the APIC_BASE. If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this field will always read 0.

IA32_MC1_STATUS.name: IA32_MC1_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error

fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error

fields.description: Threshold-based error status

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit

fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h

processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: CMCI_EN
fields.description: Software sets this bit to enable the generation of corrected machine-check error interrupt (CMCI). fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Selects the threshold at which the corrected error count logged in the status register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to the CMCI LVT entry in the APIC when the count value equals the threshold value. The new LVT entry in the APIC is at 02F0H offset from the APIC_BASE. If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this field will always read 0.

register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with

fields.name: MODEL_SPECIFIC_INFORMATION
fields.description: This field is only valid if MCI_STATUS.OTHER_INFO[1] = 1 The following bits are valid for most error types: [53]: Indicates if corresponding imc0_mc_addr has a valid channel address. For WDB parity or ECC error, following bits are valid: [7:0]: this field indicates the WDB ID For DDR ECC errors, following bits are valid: [54]: Indicates if the error was transient error; transient error is indicated for demand reads, underfill reads for partial writes, patrol and sparing reads. [52:49]: ECC mode (not valid if Bit[54] = 1) • 0001 => SDDC 128b 1LM • 0010 = SDDC 125b 1LM • 0011 = SDDC 125b 2LM • 0100 = ADDDC 80b 1LM • 0101 = ADDDC 80b 2LM • 1001 = 5x8 128b 1LM • 1010 = 5x8 125b 1LM • 1011 = 5x8 125b 2LM • b0000 = = Invalid ECC Mode [47:46]: Rank in the format as defined in RETRY_RD_ERR_lOG_ADDRESS1.CHIP_SELECT. [45:42]: CBit, with bit 45 as spare to accommodate possible future growth in size. Logged value: {1'b0,sub_rank[2:0]} [40]: In DDR mode, Sub-channel ID [39:35]: Failed device number (not valid if Bit[54] = 1 or bit[33] = 0). For non- ADDDC the device number is between 0-9. for ADDDC device number between 0-8 and 10-19 (9 is the spare device) [34]: Failed x8 half device valid (not valid if Bit[54] = 1 or bit[33] = 0): Set to 1 if failure identified is in one half device only for 5x8 DIMM. Valid for 5x8 DIMM only. [33]: Failed device valid: Set to 1 if failed device number is valid [32:30]: Bank group [29:28]: Bank address [27:10]: Row address [9:0]: Column address. Logged value is column address [11:2] or shift this field left by 2 to get real column address For MSCOD 0800h or above, following bits are valid: [22:0] will hold proprietary error info.

fields.name: ADDRESS_MODE
fields.description: Address mode for the address logged in IA32_MCi_ADDR. The supported address modes are: Segment Offset(000), Linear Address(001), Physical Address(010), Memory Address(011), Generic(111), Reserved(100 to 110)

fields.name: RECOVERABLE_ADDRESS_LSB
fields.description: The lowest valid recoverable address bit. Indicates the position of the least significant bit of the recoverable error address. For example, if the processor logs bits [43:9] of the address, the LSB sub-field is 0b01001 (9 decimal). For this example, bits [8:0] of the recoverable error address in IA32_MCi_ADDR should be ignored.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.

OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. fields.name: UC

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:

IA32_MCi_CTL register.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

IA32_MC21_STATUS.name: IA32_MC21_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: yu@int Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

fields.name: S
fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: AR
fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: THRESHOLD_BASED_STATUS
fields.description: Threshold-based error status

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit

fields.name: FW
fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator

fields.name: OTHER_INFO
fields.description: Machine Specific Architecture Error Code

fields.name: MSCOD
fields.description: Machine Check Model Specific Error Code

fields.name: MCACOD
fields.description: Machine Check Architecture Error Code

CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT_THRESHOLD:
Selects the threshold at which the corrected error count logged in the status
register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with
IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to
the CMCI LVT entry in the APIC when the count value equals the threshold value.

interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1),
this field will always read 0.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h

able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition

IA32_MC22_STATUS.name: IA32_MC22_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: yu@int Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

fields.name: S
fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: AR
fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: THRESHOLD_BASED_STATUS
fields.description: Threshold-based error status

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit

fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator

fields.description: Machine Specific Architecture Error Code

is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

[52:49]: ECC mode (not valid if Bit[54] = 1) • 0001 => SDDC 128b 1LM • 0010 = SDDC 125b 1LM • 0011 = SDDC 125b 2LM • 0100 = ADDDC 80b 1LM • 0101 = ADDDC 80b 2LM • 1001 = 5x8 128b 1LM • 1010 = 5x8 125b 1LM • 1011 = 5x8 125b 2LM • b0000 = = Invalid ECC Mode [47:46]: Rank in the format as defined in RETRY_RD_ERR_lOG_ADDRESS1.CHIP_SELECT. [45:42]: CBit, with bit 45 as spare to accommodate possible future growth in size. Logged value: {1'b0,sub_rank[2:0]} [40]: In DDR mode, Sub-channel ID [39:35]: Failed device number (not valid if Bit[54] = 1 or bit[33] = 0). For non- ADDDC the device number is between 0-9. for ADDDC device number between 0-8 and 10-19 (9 is the spare device) [34]: Failed x8 half device valid (not valid if Bit[54] = 1 or bit[33] = 0): Set to 1 if failure identified is in one half device only for 5x8 DIMM. fields.name: ADDRESS_MODE
fields.description: Address mode for the address logged in IA32_MCi_ADDR. The supported address modes are: Segment Offset(000), Linear Address(001), Physical Address(010), Memory Address(011), Generic(111), Reserved(100 to 110)

fields.name: RECOVERABLE_ADDRESS_LSB
fields.description: The lowest valid recoverable address bit. Indicates the position of the least significant bit of the recoverable error address. For example, if the processor logs bits [43:9] of the address, the LSB sub-field is 0b01001 (9 decimal). For this example, bits [8:0] of the recoverable error address in IA32_MCi_ADDR should be ignored.

over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.

fields.name: VALID

When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW

IA32_MCi_CTL register.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: CMCI_EN
fields.description: Software sets this bit to enable the generation of corrected machine-check error interrupt (CMCI). If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this bit is writeable but will always return 0 for that bank. fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Selects the threshold at which the corrected error count logged in the status register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to the CMCI LVT entry in the APIC when the count value equals the threshold value. The new LVT entry in the APIC is at 02F0H offset from the APIC_BASE. If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this field will always read 0.

fields.name: MODEL_SPECIFIC_INFORMATION
fields.description: This field is only valid if MCI_STATUS.OTHER_INFO[1] = 1 The following bits are valid for most error types: [53]: Indicates if corresponding imc0_mc_addr has a valid channel address. For WDB parity or ECC error, following bits are valid: [7:0]: this field indicates the WDB ID For DDR ECC errors, following bits are valid: [54]: Indicates if the error was transient error; transient error is indicated for demand reads, underfill reads for partial writes, patrol and sparing reads. [52:49]: ECC mode (not valid if Bit[54] = 1) • 0001 => SDDC 128b 1LM • 0010 = SDDC 125b 1LM • 0011 = SDDC 125b 2LM • 0100 = ADDDC 80b 1LM • 0101 = ADDDC 80b 2LM • 1001 = 5x8 128b 1LM • 1010 = 5x8 125b 1LM • 1011 = 5x8 125b 2LM • b0000 = = Invalid ECC Mode [47:46]: Rank in the format as defined in RETRY_RD_ERR_lOG_ADDRESS1.CHIP_SELECT. [45:42]: CBit, with bit 45 as spare to accommodate possible future growth in size. Logged value: {1'b0,sub_rank[2:0]} [40]: In DDR mode, Sub-channel ID [39:35]: Failed device number (not valid if Bit[54] = 1 or bit[33] = 0). For non- ADDDC the device number is between 0-9. for ADDDC device number between 0-8 and 10-19 (9 is the spare device) [34]: Failed x8 half device valid (not valid if Bit[54] = 1 or bit[33] = 0): Set to 1 if failure identified is in one half device only for 5x8 DIMM. Valid for 5x8 DIMM only. [33]: Failed device valid: Set to 1 if failed device number is valid [32:30]: Bank group [29:28]: Bank address [27:10]: Row address [9:0]: Column address. Logged value is column address [11:2] or shift this field left by 2 to get real column address For MSCOD 0800h or above, following bits are valid: [22:0] will hold proprietary error info.

fields.name: ADDRESS_MODE
fields.description: Address mode for the address logged in IA32_MCi_ADDR. The supported address modes are: Segment Offset(000), Linear Address(001), Physical Address(010), Memory Address(011), Generic(111), Reserved(100 to 110)

fields.name: RECOVERABLE_ADDRESS_LSB
fields.description: The lowest valid recoverable address bit. Indicates the position of the least significant bit of the recoverable error address. For example, if the processor logs bits [43:9] of the address, the LSB sub-field is 0b01001 (9 decimal). For this example, bits [8:0] of the recoverable error address in IA32_MCi_ADDR should be ignored.

VALID:

Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.

where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the

address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.

ADDRESS_MODE:
Address mode for the address logged in IA32_MCi_ADDR. The supported address
modes are: Segment Offset(000), Linear Address(001), Physical Address(010),

RECOVERABLE_ADDRESS_LSB:
The lowest valid recoverable address bit. Indicates the position of the least
significant bit of the recoverable error address. For example, if the processor logs
bits [43:9] of the address, the LSB sub-field is 0b01001 (9 decimal). For this
example, bits [8:0] of the recoverable error address in IA32_MCi_ADDR should
be ignored.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW

fields.name: CMCI_EN
fields.description: Software sets this bit to enable the generation of corrected machine-check error interrupt (CMCI). If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this bit is writeable but will always return 0 for that bank. This bit also indicates CMCI is supported or not supported in the corresponding bank.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Selects the threshold at which the corrected error count logged in the status register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to the CMCI LVT entry in the APIC when the count value equals the threshold value. The new LVT entry in the APIC is at 02F0H offset from the APIC_BASE. If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this field will always read 0.

fields.description: This field is only valid if MCI_STATUS.OTHER_INFO[1] = 1 The following bits are valid for most error types: [53]: Indicates if corresponding imc0_mc_addr has a valid channel address. flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.

OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

IA32_MC25_STATUS.name: IA32_MC25_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: yu@int Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

fields.name: S
fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: AR
fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: THRESHOLD_BASED_STATUS
fields.description: Threshold-based error status

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit

fields.name: FW
fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator

fields.name: OTHER_INFO
fields.description: Machine Specific Architecture Error Code

fields.name: MSCOD
fields.description: Machine Check Model Specific Error Code

fields.name: MCACOD
fields.description: Machine Check Architecture Error Code

the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h

able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition

IA32_MC26_STATUS.name: IA32_MC26_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: yu@int Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: AR
fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error

fields.description: Threshold-based error status

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit

fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator

fields.description: Machine Specific Architecture Error Code

register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with
IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to

interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1),
this field will always read 0.
