Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

IA32_MC27_STATUS.name: IA32_MC27_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: yu@intel.c Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

fields.name: S
fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: AR
fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: THRESHOLD_BASED_STATUS
fields.description: Threshold-based error status

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit

fields.name: FW
fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator

fields.name: OTHER_INFO
fields.description: Machine Specific Architecture Error Code

fields.name: MSCOD
fields.description: Machine Check Model Specific Error Code

fields.name: MCACOD
fields.description: Machine Check Architecture Error Code

Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

processor was able to correct the error condition

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

IA32_MC28_STATUS.name: IA32_MC28_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: R Diamond Rapids Processor-Model Specific Registers (MSRs) Registers Specification June 2026 5660 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 guohui. Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

IA32_MC29_STATUS.name: IA32_MC29_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.

IA32_MC2_STATUS.name: IA32_MC2_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: R Diamond Rapids Processor-Model Specific Registers (MSRs) Registers Specification June 2026 5566 Intel Confidential Doc. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

IA32_MC30_STATUS.name: IA32_MC30_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: yu@intel.c Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

fields.name: S
fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: AR
fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: THRESHOLD_BASED_STATUS
fields.description: Threshold-based error status

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit

fields.name: FW
fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator

fields.name: OTHER_INFO
fields.description: Machine Specific Architecture Error Code

fields.name: MSCOD
fields.description: Machine Check Model Specific Error Code

fields.name: MCACOD
fields.description: Machine Check Architecture Error Code

Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

IA32_MC31_STATUS.name: IA32_MC31_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: R Diamond Rapids Processor-Model Specific Registers (MSRs) Registers Specification June 2026 5670 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 guohui. Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

fields.name: S
fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: AR
fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error

fields.name: THRESHOLD_BASED_STATUS
fields.description: Threshold-based error status

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit

fields.name: FW
fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator

fields.name: OTHER_INFO
fields.description: Machine Specific Architecture Error Code

fields.name: MSCOD
fields.description: Machine Check Model Specific Error Code

fields.name: MCACOD
fields.description: Machine Check Architecture Error Code

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.

IA32_MC3_STATUS.name: IA32_MC3_STATUS

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: R Diamond Rapids Processor-Model Specific Registers (MSRs) Registers Specification June 2026 5570 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h

processor was able to correct the error condition

significant bit of the recoverable error address. For example, if the processor logs

and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.

OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.
57 0h
RW
PCC:
Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the
processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that
reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag
indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be
able to restart

interrupt (CMCI). If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but
IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this bit is writeable but will always return 0 for that
bank. This bit also indicates CMCI is supported or not supported in the
corresponding bank.

CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT_THRESHOLD:
Selects the threshold at which the corrected error count logged in the status
register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with
IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to
the CMCI LVT entry in the APIC when the count value equals the threshold value.
The new LVT entry in the APIC is at 02F0H offset from the APIC_BASE. If CMCI
interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1),
this field will always read 0.

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the processor was able to correct the error condition

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the IA32_MCi_CTL register.

fields.name: MISCV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor

fields.name: ADDRV
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not implemented in the processor.

fields.name: PCC
fields.description: Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be able to restart

fields.description: Signaling an uncorrected recoverable (UCR) error

fields.description: Recovery action required for Uncorrectable Recoverable (UCR) error

fields.description: Threshold-based error status

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
fields.description: Corrected error count since last clear of machine check registers. Bit 52 is a sticky overflow bit

fields.description: Firmware updated error status indicator

fields.description: Machine Specific Architecture Error Code

is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

RW

able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW

Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor

where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.

processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that
reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag
indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be
able to restart

Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

processor was able to correct the error condition

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.
57 0h
RW
PCC:
Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the
processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that
reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag
indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be
able to restart
56 0h
RW

Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: CMCI_EN
fields.description: Software sets this bit to enable the generation of corrected machine-check error interrupt (CMCI). fields.name: Reserved

fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Selects the threshold at which the corrected error count logged in the status register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to the CMCI LVT entry in the APIC when the count value equals the threshold value. The new LVT entry in the APIC is at 02F0H offset from the APIC_BASE. If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this field will always read 0.

IA32_MC7_MISC.name: IA32_MC7_MISC

fields.name: MODEL_SPECIFIC_INFORMATION
fields.description: Model-Specific Information

fields.name: ADDRESS_MODE
fields.description: Address mode for the address logged in IA32_MCi_ADDR. The supported address modes are: Segment Offset(000), Linear Address(001), Physical Address(010), Memory Address(011), Generic(111), Reserved(100 to 110)

fields.name: RECOVERABLE_ADDRESS_LSB
fields.description: The lowest valid recoverable address bit. Indicates the position of the least significant bit of the recoverable error address. For example, if the processor logs bits [43:9] of the address, the LSB sub-field is 0b01001 (9 decimal). For this example, bits [8:0] of the recoverable error address in IA32_MCi_ADDR should be ignored.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.
57 0h
RW
PCC:
Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the
processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that
reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag
indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be
able to restart

Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h

processor was able to correct the error condition

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.
57 0h
RW

Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the
processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that
reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag
indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be
able to restart

fields.name: CMCI_EN
fields.description: Software sets this bit to enable the generation of corrected machine-check error interrupt (CMCI). fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Selects the threshold at which the corrected error count logged in the status register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to the CMCI LVT entry in the APIC when the count value equals the threshold value. The new LVT entry in the APIC is at 02F0H offset from the APIC_BASE. If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this field will always read 0.

IA32_MC8_MISC.name: IA32_MC8_MISC

fields.name: MODEL_SPECIFIC_INFORMATION
fields.description: Model-Specific Information

fields.name: ADDRESS_MODE
fields.description: Address mode for the address logged in IA32_MCi_ADDR. The supported address modes are: Segment Offset(000), Linear Address(001), Physical Address(010), Memory Address(011), Generic(111), Reserved(100 to 110)

fields.name: RECOVERABLE_ADDRESS_LSB
fields.description: The lowest valid recoverable address bit. Indicates the position of the least significant bit of the recoverable error address. For example, if the processor logs bits [43:9] of the address, the LSB sub-field is 0b01001 (9 decimal). For this example, bits [8:0] of the recoverable error address in IA32_MCi_ADDR should be ignored.

the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.

rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: VALID
fields.description: Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries. The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.

fields.name: OVERFLOW
fields.description: Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors. Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: UC

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred
61 0h
RW
UC:
Uncorrected Error: Indicates (when set) that the processor did not or was not
able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition
60 0h
RW
EN:
Indicates (when set) that the error was enabled by the associated EEj bit of the
IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h
RW
MISCV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor
58 0h
RW
ADDRV:
Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_ADDR register contains the address
where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.
57 0h
RW
PCC:
Processor Context Corrupted. Indicates (when set) that the state of the
processor might have been corrupted by the error condition detected and that
reliable restarting of the processor may not be possible. When clear, this flag
indicates that the error did not affect the processors state, and software may be
able to restart
56 0h

Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

able to correct the error condition. When clear, this flag indicates that the
processor was able to correct the error condition

IA32_MCi_CTL register.
59 0h

Indicates (when set) that the IA32_MCi_MISC register contains additional
information regarding the error. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_MISC register is either not implemented or does not contain additional
information regarding the error. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor

where the error occurred. When clear, this flag indicates that the
IA32_MCi_ADDR register is either not implemented or does not contain the
address where the error occurred. Do not read these registers if they are not
implemented in the processor.

VALID:
Indicates (when set) that the information within the IA32_MCi_STATUS register
is valid. When this flag is set, the processor follows the rules given for the OVER
flag in the IA32_MCi_STATUS register when overwriting previously valid entries.
The processor sets the VAL flag and software is responsible for clearing it.
62 0h
RW
OVERFLOW:
Error Overflow: Indicates (when set) that a machine-check error occurred while
the results of a previous error were still in the error-reporting register bank (that
is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

fields.name: CMCI_EN
fields.description: Software sets this bit to enable the generation of corrected machine-check error interrupt (CMCI). fields.name: CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Selects the threshold at which the corrected error count logged in the status register will signal an interrupt. The value is compared with IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT. An overflow event is signaled to the CMCI LVT entry in the APIC when the count value equals the threshold value. The new LVT entry in the APIC is at 02F0H offset from the APIC_BASE. If CMCI interface is not supported for a particular bank (but IA32_MCG_CAP[10] = 1), this field will always read 0.

fields.description: The lowest valid recoverable address bit. Indicates the position of the least significant bit of the recoverable error address. is, IA32_MCi_STATUS.VAL was already set). The processor sets the OVER flag
and software is responsible for clearing it. In general, enabled errors are written
over disabled errors, and uncorrected errors are written over corrected errors.
Uncorrected errors are not written over previous valid uncorrected errors. When
MCG_CMCI_P is set, corrected errors may not set the OVER flag. Software can
rely on corrected error count in IA32_MCi_STATUS.CORRECTED_ERROR_COUNT
to determine if any additional corrected errors may have occurred

processor was able to correct the error condition

LBESTS1.name: LBESTS1
sections: Leaky Bucket Error LBESTS1 The Leaky Bucket counter increments the following correctable error types:

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: /P
fields.description: Lane Error Status (LNERRSTS): Lane(s) in which errors have been seen since entering this data rate (unless frozen) and contributed to the current ERRCNT.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: RATE
fields.description: The data rate that the values in Leaky Bucket Status 1 and 2 apply to. This will be the current rate unless the LBE Enable has been cleared (manually or through a freeze event). 0 - 2.5GT/s 1 - 5GT/s .. 4 - 32GT/s

fields.name: ERRCNT
fields.description: This register represents the current count of errors. It increments by one for each clock cycle with one or more receiver errors. It decrements by one at the rate defined by the relevant data rate's drip rate. Increments will not cause a rollover and decrements will not cause a roll under.

fields.name: LEAKY_BKT_2ND_CNTR_LIMIT
fields.description: Secondary Leaky Bucket Counter Limit (2b per DIMM). This register defines secondary leaky bucket counter limit for all 4 logical ranks within a subchannel channel. The counter logic will generate the secondary LEAK pulse to decrement the ranks correctable error counter by 1 when the corresponding rank leaky bucket rank counter roll over at the predefined counter limit. The counter increment at the primary leak pulse from the LEAKY_BUCKET_CNTR_LO and LEAKY_BUCKET_CNTR_HI logic. Bit [23:22]: Rank 3 Secondary Leaky Bucket Counter Limit Bit [21:20]: Rank 2 Secondary Leaky Bucket Counter Limit Bit [19:18]: Rank 1 Secondary Leaky Bucket Counter Limit Bit [17:16]: Rank 0 Secondary Leaky Bucket Counter Limit The value of the limit is defined as the following: the LEAK pulse is generated after a primary LEAK pulse is received when the rank's corresponding counter in leaky_bkt_2nd_cntr has the value of leaky_bkt_2nd_cntr_limit - 1. When leaky_bkt_2nd_cntr_limit for the rank is 0, it represent the value of 4. After LEAK pulse is generated, the counter is reset to 0. Assuming N = leaky_bkt_2nd_cntr_limit per rank, with N = 4 if leaky_bkt_2nd_cntr_limit = 0, a LEAK pulse is generated every N primary LEAK pulse.

fields.name: LEAKY_BKT_2ND_CNTR
fields.description: Per rank secondary leaky bucket counter (2b per rank) Bit [7:6]: Rank 3 secondary leaky bucket counter Bit [5:4]: Rank 2 secondary leaky bucket counter Bit [3:2]: Rank 1 secondary leaky bucket counter Bit [1:0]: Rank 0 secondary leaky bucket counter

fields.name: BIST_CORR_MODE
fields.description: When set to 1, PFD is used to correct single device DUE case. If this bit is set to 1, bist_err_report_mode bit should be programmed to 0.

fields.name: BIST_CE_CORRFSM_NOERR
fields.description: This bit is used to program the final result for the case when PFD gives CE and correction fsm gives NoErorr. Values it can take are: 00 -> UC 01 -> CE 10 -> NoError (Recommended)

fields.name: BIST_ERR_REPORT_MODE
fields.description: This bit is used to select PFD to work in Error Reporting Mode. In this mode, only PFD results are logged, but they are not considered to make the final decision in the ECC correction path.

fields.name: BIST_EN
fields.description: This bit is used to enable PFD (Permanent Fault Detection) in the ECC correction path.

fields.description: This is the higher order bit select mask of the two hot encoding threshold. fields.name: LEAKY_BKT_CNTR_LO
fields.description: This is the lower half of the leaky bucket counter. The full counter is actually a 53b HCLK counter. There is a least significant 11b of the 53b counter is not captured in CSR. The carry strobe from the not-shown least significant 11b counter will trigger this 42b counter pair to count. The 42b counter-pair is compared with the two-hot encoding threshold specified by the LEAKY_BUCKET_CFG_HI and LEAKY_BUCKET_CFG_LO pair. When the counter bits specified by the LEAKY_BUCKET_CFG_HI and LEAKY_BUCKET_CFG_LO are both set, the 53b counter is reset and the leaky bucket logic will generate a LEAK strobe last for 1 HCLK.

strobe last for 1 HCLK.

fields.name: TLPHDRLOG
fields.description: As soon as an error is logged in this register, it remains locked for further error- logging until the software clears the status bit that caused the header log (in other words, until the error pointer is re-armed for logging again).

fields.name: NEXT_ID_BLOCK_OFFSET
fields.description: This field allows for custom extensions of IP Identification information per IP. A value of 00h identifies this as the terminal structure. A non-zero value represents a byte offset into the current address space relative to the IP Base address where the next IP Identification Register Block can be found.

fields.name: IP_CAPABILITY_IDENTIFIER
fields.description: IP ID Block Capability Identifier: 0h - Reserved; 1h - IP Version Structure; 2h- FFh - Reserved

fields.name: ID_BLOCK_VERSION
fields.description: Version of this IPID Register Block Type. For this version of the implementation a value of 0x1 is required for this field.

fields.description: IP ID Block Capability Identifier: 0h - Reserved; 1h - IP Version Structure; 2h-FFh - Reserved.

fields.name: LINK_FAIL_SEL_CMCI
fields.description: When enabled (set to 1), link fail is logged and signaled as Corr error, and included in Corrected Error Count; when disabled (cleared to 0), link fail is logged and signaled as fatal error (uc = 1, pcc = 1) and not included in Corrected Error Count. This bit is usually set to 1 for full mirroring mode only. Note, normal signal rule based on error type is followed.

fields.name: TPAR_RECOV
fields.description: Maximum value of ALERT_n pulse width as specified in JEDEC, in number of HCLK, minus 127. 127 should be subtracted after the pulse width is converted to HCLK. Maximum ALERT_n pulse width includes PRAC ALERT_n pulse width, when it is enabled. If the subtraction result in a value less than 1 (HCLK), use the value of 1.

fields.name: BLOCK_VERSION
fields.description: Version of this IPID Register Block Type.

fields.name: ERF_EN0
fields.description: This should be set to 1 to enable link error flow.

LINK_RETRY_TIMER.name: LINK_RETRY_TIMER
sections: Correctable error (UC=0, PCC=0) for data UC errors corrected by FM fill.

fields.name: RESET_LINK_ERR_CNT
fields.description: Hardware resets the error counters when this bit changes from a 0 to 1.

fields.name: SB_ERR_OBSERVATION_TIME
fields.description: Error observation window (in units of link_err_flow_time_unit * 2 ^ sb_err_observation_time) during which number of alerts are counted when link error FSM is ready to accept new error (a.k.a. transient error). The error window resulted from this register gets divided by 2 in hardware to use the link_err_flow_time_unit as DCLK duration. As a result a value of 0 is not allowed. Change from default value to enable link fail. BIOS will need to program this CSR correctly after reset. Recommendation is to set this field, along with link_err_flow_time_unit, to make the observation window as 1000 seconds.

fields.name: LINK_ERR_FLOW_TIME_UNIT
fields.description: Holds the tick amount (specified in DCLKs) for the error observation window timers, it serves as a base counter, each time the counter hits the CSR value, one is added to the counter for observation window. Program a non-zero value when link fail is enabled. Diamond Rapids Processor June 2026 Registers Specification Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 Intel Confidential 4863

fields.name: LFET1S
fields.description: This field is set by hardware if a Link Fatal Error Type 1 condition is detected on the eSPI link (any transaction). Note: Clearing this unlocks and sets to default value the LFET1C field and triggers a deassert_SMI flow from eSPI service to SMI service if LFET1E is set to SMI. Note: Setting of this bit is independent of the enable to generate a SMI/SERR (LFET1E). Reset Source: Register bit is reset on IA cold reset

fields.name: LFET1C
fields.description: • 0h: No error • 1h: eSPI-Device Response Code: NO_RESPONSE (Type 1) • 2h: eSPI-Device Response Code: FATAL_ERROR (Type 1) • 3h: eSPI-Device Response Code: CRC_ERROR (Type 1) • 4h: Invalid eSPI-Device Response Code (w.r.t. to Command) (Type 1) • 5h: Invalid eSPI-Device Cycle Type (w.r.t. to Command) (Type 1) • 6h: Malformed eSPI-Device Response Payload: Payload length > Max Payload Size (Type 1) Note: This field is updated to default value by clearing (1C) OF LFET1S. Reset Source: Register bit is reset on IA warm reset

fields.name: LFET1CTYP
fields.description: When LFET1C is set, this field reflects the Cycle Type for the transaction that encountered the Fatal Error Type 1. Note: This field is updated after a transaction (any channel) is completed if the LFET1S bit is clear. Reset Source: Register bit is reset on IA warm reset

fields.name: LFET1CMD
fields.description: RSecure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers-Diamond Rapids Processor When LFET1C is set, this field reflects the Command for the transaction that encountered the Fatal Error Type 1. Note: This field is updated after a transaction (any channel) is completed if the LFET1S bit is clear. Reset Source: Register bit is reset on IA warm reset

NMICSTS.name: NMICSTS

fields.name: NMI_VLW_STS
fields.description: A writeable status bit which is set whenever a VLW message that assert NMI is successfuly sent and the associated completion is received. Its intent is to enable a pooling mechanism for software to enforce NMI_NOW message ordering. Once set, writing the bit to1 will clear the status. Writing ithe bit to 0 has no effect. For cases where the delivery of the VLW message is blocked (NMI Enable not asserted, NMI2SMI enable asserted, Sideband hosting disabled, Force PowerGate pending), the setting of the delivery status bit will be held until the delivery of the NMI VLW message actually occurs. It will be the responsibility of the puller to understand if any of these conditions exist. Note: pmc_allow_vlw is tied to 1 on S3M IBL based system.

fields.name: NMI_STS
fields.description: RO status bit indicating the current state of the ITSS internal NMI wire. It is set to (1'b1) whenever the following is met: • any NMI source has asserted NMI • IO Port 70 NMI_EN# bit is asserted (1'b0) • NMI2SMI_EN is cleared (1'b0)

fields.name: NMI2SMI_STS
fields.description: RO status bit indicating the current state of the ITSS internal NMI2SMI wire. It is set to (1'b1) whenever the following is met: • any NMI source has asserted NMI • IO Port 70 NMI_EN# bit is asserted (1'b0) • NMI2SMI_EN is set (1'b1)

fields.name: NMI2SMI_EN
fields.description: Setting to 1b1 causes NMIs to be sent as ASSERT_SMI/DEASSERT_SMI messages to PMC instead of the regular NMI messages. Setting to 1b0 maintains the regular NMI routing (as VLW and VM). Bits NMI_NOW and NMI2SMI_EN can't be configurated on same cycle. Note:Parameter Controlled: ITSS only uses this CR based value of NMI2SMI_EN when its top-level parameter USE_NMI_CTRL_REG != 0. Otherwise, the current NMI2SMI_EN value is located as a physical register in the Host SMBus Controller and is communicated to ITSS via the top-level input pin mu1_smnmi2smi_en. When USE_NMI_CTRL_REG = 0, writing this CR bit will not affect ITSS operations. Note: USE_NMI_CTRL_REG parameter is set to '1' for Integrated Boot System.

fields.name: NMI_NOW_STS
fields.description: RO status bit indicating the current state of NMI_NOW. See NMI_NOW.

fields.name: NMI_NOW
fields.description: Writing 1b1 to NMI_NOW inverts the NMI NOW Status (NMI_NOW_STS) value. The first time NMI_NOW is written sets the NMI_NOW_STS and initiates an NMI. The next write clears the NMI_NOW_STS and allows initiating NMI by the next write to NMI_NOW. Writing 1b0 to NMI_NOW has no effect. Bits NMI_NOW and NMI2SMI_EN can't be configurated on same cycle. Note: Parameter Controlled: ITSS only uses this CR based value of NMI_NOW when its top-level parameter USE_NMI_CTRL_REG != 0. PATROL_TAD_RULE.name: PATROL_TAD_RULE
sections: Correctable error (UC=0, PCC=0) for data UC errors corrected by FM fill.

fields.name: PATROL_TAD_EN
fields.description: This TAD rule is enabled. BIOS should set patrol_tad_en=0 to skip this TAD from being scrubbed.

fields.name: IGN_PTRL_UC
fields.description: Downgrades patrol scrubbing uncorrectable errors to correctable for this TAD range.

fields.name: IS_TO_NM
fields.description: This TAD rule is used for 2LM NM. Different ECC mode is used and error is handled differently for 2LM NM.

fields.name: CA_LIMIT
fields.description: Corresponding TAD limit address in Channel Address with 64MB granularity. This field should be programmed as bits 40:26 of last channel address of the current TAD. Lower bits not included in this field have value of all 1s. Note, it is required to have patrol_tad_rule[N+1].ca_limit >= patrol_tad_rule[N].ca_limit for proper operation, even if the given patrol_tad_rule is not enabled (patrol_tad_en = 0). It is recommended to leave unused patrol_tad_rule at HW default value (this excludes including used but disabled rules).

fields.name: REGION_SIZE
fields.description: This field selects the granularity for the sparing copy operation: 00=Bank 01=Rank 1X=Reserved

fields.name: ADDDC_SPARING
fields.description: This bit causes the sparing copy to be ADDDC sparing when sparing copy has been started via the spare_enable bit. This register is locked by the DISABLE_ADDDC_SPARING bit from IMC_FUSE_DOWNLOAD register.

fields.name: REVERSE_SPARE
fields.description: Setting this bit will cause sparing engine to be run in reverse (e.g., move from virtual lockstep back to independent) when sparing has been started via the spare_enable bit. Example usage cases are upgrading a region failure from bank to rank, or unpair existing ADDDC pair to repair with different rank/bank, or testing.

fields.name: ENABLE_SPARE
fields.description: Enable ADDDC sparing copy when set to 1. Hardware clears this bit after the sparing completion.
