PCERR_SLV0.name: PCERR_SLV0

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: SLV_HOST_RST_ACK_OVRD
fields.description: A 1 in this bit will cause the eSPI Host Controller to not wait for the Device HOST_RESET_ACK Virtual Wire. The Host_Reset_Warn VW will be transmitted to the Device independent of the setting for this bit. Reset Source: Register is reset on IA Warm Reset.

fields.name: PCRMTARE
fields.description: • 2'b00: Disable RMA or RTA Reporting • 2'b01: Reserved • 2'b10: Enable RMA or RTA Reporting as SERR (IOSF-SB Do_SErr message) • 2'b11: Enable RMA or RTA Reporting as SMI (IOSF-SB Assert_SMI message) Note: SERR enable is also qualified by PCCMD.SEE (Offset 04h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. Note: SERR also sets PCSTS.SSE (Offset 06h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. BIOS programs these registers per specific platform requirement. Reset Source: Register is reset on IA Warm Reset.

fields.name: PCURRE
fields.description: If set to 1 by software, it allows reporting of an Unsupported Request (UR) as a System Error (SERR). If eSPI controller decodes a Posted transaction that is not supported, it sets the PCURD bit. If PCCMD.SEE (SERR enable) is also set to 1, then eSPIMC sets the PCSTS.SSE (Signaled System Error) bit and sends a Do_SERR message. Note: If the transaction was a Non-Posted request, then the agent handles the transaction as an Advisory Non-Fatal error, and no error logging or signaling is done. The Completion with UR Completion Status serves the purpose of error reporting. Reset Source: Register is reset on IA Warm Reset. RSecure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers-Diamond Rapids Processor

fields.name: PCURD
fields.description: Set to 1 by eSPI-Host upon detecting an Unspported Request (UR) that is not considered an Advisory Non- Fatal error and PCERR.PCURRE is set. Cleared to 0 when software writes a 1 to this register. Reset Source: Register is reset on IA Warm Reset.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: PCNFEE
fields.description: • 00: Disable Non-Fatal Error Reporting • 01: Reserved • 10: Enable Non-Fatal Error Reporting as SERR • 11: Enable Non-Fatal Error Reporting as SMI Note: SERR enable is also qualified by PCCMD.SEE (Offset 04h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. Note: SERR also sets PCSTS.SSE (Offset 06h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. Note: SMI/SERR messages are not generated if the Host is in reset (PLTRST# asserted). Reset Source: Register is reset on IA warm reset

fields.name: PCNFES
fields.description: This field is set by hardware if a Non-Fatal Error condition is detected on the Peripheral Channel. Software must clear this bit. • 0: No Non-Fatal Error detected • 1: Non-Fatal Error detected (PCNFEC has a non-zero value) Note: Clearing this unlocks and sets to default value the PCNFEC field and triggers an IOSF-SB Deassert_SMI message if PCNFEE is set to SMI. Note: Setting of this bit is independent of the enable to generate a SMI/SERR (PCNFEE). Reset Source: Register is reset on IA warm reset

fields.name: PCNFEC
fields.description: • 0h: No error • 1h: eSPI-Device Response Code: NONFATAL_ERROR • 2h: eSPI-Device Cycle Type: Unsuccessful Completion • 3h: Unexpected completion received from eSPI-Device (i.e. completion without non-posted request or completion with invalid tag or completion with invalid length) • 5h: Unsupported Message Code • 8h-Fh: Reserved Note: This field is updated to default value by clearing (1C) of PCNFES. Reset Source: Register is reset on IA warm reset

fields.name: PMMA
fields.description: Applies to only posted and non-posted memory transactions directed towards D31:f0 to be sent over the eSPI Peripheral Channel to an eSPI Device • 1'b0: Requests with a length of 3 bytes or requests with a length of 1/2/4 bytes whose Address+Length is not DWord aligned will be rejected. • 1'b1: Requests with a length of 3 bytes or requests with a lenght of 1/2/4 butes whose Address+Length is not DWord aligned will be sent to the Device using the memory write/read format. Reset Source: Register is reset on IA warm reset

fields.name: PCFEE
fields.description: • 00: Disable Fatal Error Reporting • 01: Reserved • 10: Enable Fatal Error Reporting as SERR (Do_SERR message) R Diamond Rapids Processor-Secure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers Registers Specification June 2026 1694 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 • 11: Enable Fatal Error Reporting as SMI (Assert_SMI from eSPI service to SMI service) Note: SERR enable is also qualified by PCCMD.SEE (Offset 04h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. Note: SERR also sets PCSTS.SSE (Offset 06h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. Note: SMI/SERR messages are not generated if the Host is in reset (PLTRST# asserted). Reset Source: Register is reset on IA cold reset Note: This is reserved on S3M IBL as scratchpad with no function since PCFES is always Read Only as 1'b0.

fields.name: PCFES
fields.description: This field is set by eSPI-Host if a Fatal Error condition is detected on the Peripheral Channel. Software must clear this bit by writing a 1 to it. • 0: No Fatal Error detected • 1: Fatal Error (Type 1) detected (PCFEC has a non-zero value) Note: Clearing this unlocks the PCFEC field and triggers a deassert_SMI flow from eSPI service to SMI service if PCFEE is set to SMI. Note: Setting of this bit is independent of the enable to generate a SMI/SERR (PCFEE). Reset Source: Register is reset on IA cold reset Note: This is reserved on S3M IBL as there is no separate Fatal Error Cause that will set PCFES.

fields.name: PCFEC
fields.description: • 0h: No error • 1h - 7h: Reserved • Bh - Fh: Reserved Reset Source: Register is reset on IA cold reset

PCERR_SLV1.name: PCERR_SLV1

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: SLV_HOST_RST_ACK_OVRD
fields.description: RSecure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers-Diamond Rapids Processor A 1 in this bit will cause the eSPI Host Controller to not wait for the Device HOST_RESET_ACK Virtual Wire. The Host_Reset_Warn VW will be transmitted to the Device independent of the setting for this bit. Reset Source: Register is reset on IA Warm Reset.

fields.name: PCRMTARE
fields.description: • 2'b00: Disable RMA or RTA Reporting • 2'b01: Reserved • 2'b10: Enable RMA or RTA Reporting as SERR (IOSF-SB Do_SErr message) • 2'b11: Enable RMA or RTA Reporting as SMI (IOSF-SB Assert_SMI message) Note: SERR enable is also qualified by PCCMD.SEE (Offset 04h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. Note: SERR also sets PCSTS.SSE (Offset 06h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. BIOS programs these registers per specific platform requirement. Reset Source: Register is reset on IA Warm Reset.

fields.name: PCURRE
fields.description: If set to 1 by software, it allows reporting of an Unsupported Request (UR) as a System Error (SERR). If eSPI controller decodes a Posted transaction that is not supported, it sets the PCURD bit. If PCCMD.SEE (SERR enable) is also set to 1, then eSPIMC sets the PCSTS.SSE (Signaled System Error) bit and sends a Do_SERR message. Note: If the transaction was a Non-Posted request, then the agent handles the transaction as an Advisory Non-Fatal error, and no error logging or signaling is done. The Completion with UR Completion Status serves the purpose of error reporting. Reset Source: Register is reset on IA Warm Reset.

fields.name: PCURD
fields.description: Set to 1 by eSPI-Host upon detecting an Unspported Request (UR) that is not considered an Advisory Non- Fatal error and PCERR.PCURRE is set. Cleared to 0 when software writes a 1 to this register. Reset Source: Register is reset on IA Warm Reset.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: PCNFEE
fields.description: • 00: Disable Non-Fatal Error Reporting • 01: Reserved • 10: Enable Non-Fatal Error Reporting as SERR • 11: Enable Non-Fatal Error Reporting as SMI Note: SERR enable is also qualified by PCCMD.SEE (Offset 04h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. Note: SERR also sets PCSTS.SSE (Offset 06h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. Note: SMI/SERR messages are not generated if the Host is in reset (PLTRST# asserted). Reset Source: Register is reset on IA warm reset

fields.name: PCNFES
fields.description: This field is set by hardware if a Non-Fatal Error condition is detected on the Peripheral Channel. Software must clear this bit. • 0: No Non-Fatal Error detected • 1: Non-Fatal Error detected (PCNFEC has a non-zero value) Note: Clearing this unlocks and set the default value the PCNFEC field and triggers an IOSF-SB Deassert_SMI message if PCNFEE is set to SMI. Note: Setting of this bit is independent of the enable to generate a SMI/SERR (PCNFEE). Reset Source: Register is reset on IA warm reset R Diamond Rapids Processor-Secure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers Registers Specification June 2026 1696 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15

fields.name: PCNFEC
fields.description: • 0h: No error • 1h: eSPI-Device Response Code: NONFATAL_ERROR • 2h: eSPI-Device Cycle Type: Unsuccessful Completion • 3h: Unexpected completion received from eSPI-Device (i.e. completion without non-posted request or completion with invalid tag or completion with invalid length) • 5h: Unsupported Message Code • 8h-Fh: Reserved Note: This field is updated to default value by clearing (1C) of PCNFES. Reset Source: Register is reset on IA warm reset

fields.name: PMMA
fields.description: Applies to only posted and non-posted memory transactions directed towards D31:f0 to be sent over the eSPI Peripheral Channel to an eSPI Device • 1'b0: Requests with a length of 3 bytes or requests with a length of 1/2/4 bytes whose Address+Length is not DWord aligned will be rejected. • 1'b1: Requests with a length of 3 bytes or requests with a lenght of 1/2/4 butes whose Address+Length is not DWord aligned will be sent to the Device using the memory write/read format. Reset Source: Register is reset on IA warm reset

fields.name: PCFEE
fields.description: • 00: Disable Fatal Error Reporting • 01: Reserved • 10: Enable Fatal Error Reporting as SERR (Do_SERR message) • 11: Enable Fatal Error Reporting as SMI (Assert_SMI from eSPI service to SMI service) Note: SERR enable is also qualified by PCCMD.SEE (Offset 04h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. Note: SERR also sets PCSTS.SSE (Offset 06h) when PLTRST# is deasserted. Note: SMI/SERR messages are not generated if the Host is in reset (PLTRST# asserted). Reset Source: Register is reset on IA cold reset Note: This is reserved on S3M IBL as scratchpad with no function since PCFES is always Read Only as 1'b0.

fields.name: PCFES
fields.description: This field is set by eSPI-Host if a Fatal Error condition is detected on the Peripheral Channel. Software must clear this bit by writing a 1 to it. • 0: No Fatal Error detected • 1: Fatal Error (Type 1) detected (PCFEC has a non-zero value) Note: Clearing this unlocks the PCFEC field and triggers a deassert_SMI flow from eSPI service to SMI service if PCFEE is set to SMI. Note: Setting of this bit is independent of the enable to generate a SMI/SERR (PCFEE). Reset Source: Register is reset on IA cold reset Note: This is reserved on S3M IBL as there is no separate Fatal Error Cause that will set PCFES.

fields.name: PCFEC
fields.description: • 0h: No error • 1h - 7h: Reserved • Bh - Fh: Reserved Reset Source: Register is reset on IA cold reset RSecure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers-Diamond Rapids Processor

sections: Completer Abort Error Conditions PCISTS_PCICMD PCISTS_PCICMD PCISTS_PCICMD

fields.name: SSE
fields.description: This bit is set when the device has detected an un-correctable error and reported it via SERR message. This requires SERR Enable bit to be set in Command register.

fields.name: STA
fields.description: Set by the device when aborting a request that violates the device programming model. When SERR Enable is set SERR message will be sent.

fields.name: CAPLIST
fields.description: Indicates that a device implements extended capabilities. Hardwired to 0 because there are no capability list structures in this function.

fields.name: INTR_STATUS
fields.description: The Interrupt Status field is a RO field that indicates that an interrupt message is pending internally to the device.

fields.name: INT_DISABLE
fields.description: Controls the ability of a device to generate a legacy interrupt message. When set, the device cannot generate legacy interrupt messages. Note: No Interrupt generated from the device. Reserved as RW with no function impact.

fields.name: SERR_ENABLE
fields.description: 1 = Enables SERR# generation

fields.name: BME
fields.description: Bus Driver Enable does not apply to messages sent out by PMC. This bit is reset by PLTRST# assertion.

fields.name: MSE
fields.description: Memory Space Enable Controls a device's response to Memory Space accesses. This bit controls whether the host to ACPI device MMIO BAR is enabled or not. This bit is reset by PLTRST# assertion

fields.name: IOSE
fields.description: 1= enables access to the I/O space registers as defined by the Base Address Register. Diamond Rapids Processor Registers Specification June 2026 1594 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15

RETRY_RD_ERR_LOG.name: RETRY_RD_ERR_LOG
sections: Correctable error (UC=0, PCC=0) for data UC errors corrected by FM fill.

During the last log, entered correction, error was in device 9 for 10x4 SDDC, or left half of device 4 for 5x8 ECC, or parity device for Adaptive Double DeviceDataCorrection (ADDDC)ECC. For 5x8, there
Error Intel® Xeon® 6900/6700/6500- D70 D60 D50 D40 D30 D20 D10 D00

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: ECC_BIST_ERRTYPE
fields.description: Indicates the err type for the PFD result. Valid only if ecc_bist_valid field is true in the retry_rd_err_log. PFD Result No Error = 2'b00 PFD Result UE (Multi-Device Corruption or Inconsistent) = 2'b01 PFD Result CE (Single Device Corruption) = 2'b10 This result may be not the same as the final correction result.

fields.name: CORR_FSM_ERRTYPE
fields.description: Indicates the err type for the Correction FSM result. No Error = 2'b00 Uncorrectable = 2'b01 Correctable = 2'b10 This isn't logged when in PFD bypass mode or error reporting mode as the retry_rd_err_log contents represents only the Correction FSM results in these modes.

fields.name: ECC_BIST_VALID
fields.description: Indicates that PFD is used for the logged error. The fields ecc_bist_errtype, ecc_bist_corr_err_devnum, and any other PFD related fields in retry_rd_err_log registers are only valid if this is true.

fields.name: SYSTEM_ADDR_VALID
fields.description: Indicates there is valid system address in the retry_rd_err_address3_log register.

fields.name: PERSISTENT_ERROR
fields.description: Indicates persistent single device error is detected by PFD.

fields.name: TRANSFER_NUMBER
fields.description: Indicates Transfer number of the single bit correction. This field is only valid with single bit correctable error for non-ADDDC ECC mode (i.e., when single_bit_error is set to 1).

fields.name: SINGLE_BIT_ERROR
fields.description: RMemory Controller (MC) Registers-Diamond Rapids Processor For DDR mode, indicates if there was a single bit correction for non-ADDDC ECC mode. This field is only valid with correctable error.

fields.name: COL_CORRECTION
fields.description: For DDR mode, this field indicate a column correction done instead of the device correction and is only valid for ADDDC 80b mode. In all other DDR ECC modes, this field should be ignored. This field is only valid with correctable errors.

fields.name: BIST_CORR
fields.description: For 10x4 125b SDDC single device corruption, set to 1 by HW when failed device cannot be determined by ECC algorithm, and correction is done using PFD determined failed device. Also set to 1 by HW for such corruption case if correction is done using sparing failed device during sparing.

fields.name: NOOVER
fields.description: Lock register after the first correctable error; do not overwrite for subsequent correctable errors. Uncorrectable errors will overwrite the correctable error information in retry_rd_err_log registers even if this bit is set.

fields.name: EN_PATSPR
fields.description: If en_patspr=1: Log patrol/sparing read errors and NOT demand/underfill read errors; if en_patspr=0: Log demand/underfill read errors and NOT patrol/sparing read errors. Default is to log demand/underfill read errors.

fields.name: PATSPR
fields.description: If patspr=1, a patrol/spare error was logged.

fields.name: EN
fields.description: Enable error logging. Will log on every retry if type matches.

fields.name: CORR_CORRECTABLE_PAR_DEV
fields.description: During the last log, entered correction, error was in device 9 for 10x4 SDDC, or left half of device 4 for 5x8 ECC, or parity device for ADDDC ECC. For 5x8, there could also be error in right half of device 4 but this bit is not set. This field is only valid with correctable error. Not valid for 9x4.

fields.name: CORR_CORRECTABLE
fields.description: During the last log, entered correction, detected a correctable ecc error and corrected the error.

fields.name: CORR_NOERR
fields.description: During the last log, entered correction but no ecc error was detected.

fields.name: CORR_ERR
fields.description: During the last log, entered correction but was not able to correct the error => DUE.

fields.name: SYSTEM_ADDR_ERR
fields.description: System address translation error.

fields.name: MODE
fields.description: Indicate the ECC mode for error logged in the corresponding retry_rd_err_log* registers: DDR ECC mode: 4'b0001 => SDDC 128b 1LM 4'b0010 => SDDC 125b 1LM 4'b0011 => SDDC 125b 2LM 4'b0100 => ADDDC 80b 1LM 4'b0101 => ADDDC 80b 2LM 4'b0110 => 9x4 64b 1LM 4'b0111 => 9x4 61b 1LM 4'b1000 => 9x4 61b 2LM 4'b1001 => 5x8 128b 1LM R Diamond Rapids Processor-Memory Controller (MC) Registers Registers Specification June 2026 4628 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 4'b1010 => 5x8 125b 1LM 4'b1011 => 5x8 125b 2LM 4'b0000 => Invalid ECC Mode

fields.name: OVER
fields.description: The log has been overwritten.

fields.name: UC
fields.description: Uncorrectable error.

fields.name: V
fields.description: The contents of this register have valid data as well as RETRY_RD_ERR_LOG_PARITY, RETRY_RD_ERR_LOG_PARITY_HI, RETRY_RD_ERR_LOG_MISC, RETRY_RD_ERR_LOG_ADDRESS1, RETRY_RD_ERR_LOG_ADDRESS2 and RETRY_RD_ERR_LOG_ADDRESS3.

fields.name: CHANNEL_ADDR_VALID
fields.description: Indicates there is valid channel address in the retry_rd_err_address3_log register.

fields.name: FAILED_DEV_VALID
fields.description: Failing device is identified and logged failed_dev is valid. For ADDDC mode, logged rank/subrank/bank matches the failing device location when this bit is set.

fields.name: COL
fields.description: Column address bits for the last retry. In DDR mode, logged value is column address [11:2] or shift this field left by 2 to get real column address.

fields.name: BA
fields.description: BA for last retry.

fields.name: BG
fields.description: BG for last retry.

fields.name: CBIT
fields.description: C0-C2 (encoded subrank) for last retry. Logged value is {2'b0,cbit[2:0]}.

fields.name: CHIP_SELECT
fields.description: RMemory Controller (MC) Registers-Diamond Rapids Processor Rank for last retry. In native DDR5 mode, bit 1 is the DIMM index and bit 0 is the rank index. In MRDIMM mode, bit 1 is the rank index and bit 0 is the pseudo- channel index.

fields.name: FAILED_DEV
fields.description: Holds the failed device number: for 10x4 SDDC, the device number is between 0-9. For 9x4 ECC, the device number is between 0-8. For 5x8 ECC, the device number is also between 0-9 if failure identified within one half device (when retry_rd_err_log_misc.x8_half_dev_valid = 1). If failure is not within one half x8 device (retry_rd_err_log_misc.x8_half_dev_valid = 0), then the device number would be 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. This means the x8 device has corruption in both halves. For x8 DIMM, failed_dev[3:1] represent x8 device number and failed_dev[0] indicates which half the failure is in (when available). For ADDDC device number between 0-8 and 10-19 with dev 9 being the spare device. In ADDDC mode, this field is only valid with correctable error of the type device correction.

fields.name: ECC_BIST_CORR_ERR_DEVNUM
fields.description: R Diamond Rapids Processor-Memory Controller (MC) Registers Registers Specification June 2026 4632 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 Holds the failed device number for PFD result when single device corruption is detected: for 10x4 SDDC, the device number is between 0-9. For 9x4 ECC, the device number is between 0-8. For 5x8 ECC, the device number is also between 0-9 if failure identified within one half device (when retry_rd_err_log_address2.ecc_bist_corr_err_x8_half_dev_valid = 1). If failure is not within one half x8 device (retry_rd_err_log_address2.ecc_bist_corr_err_x8_half_dev_valid = 0), then the device number would be 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. This means the x8 device has corruption in both halves. For x8 ECC, ecc_bist_corr_err_devnum[3:1] represent x8 device number and failed_dev[0] indicates which half the failure is in (when available). Valid only when ecc_bist_valid is true and ecc_bist_errtype is PFD Result CE.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: ADDR_PAR_ERR
fields.description: System or channel address has parity error in internal RF storage and is not valid.

fields.name: RAS_UNDETERMINED
fields.description: Set to 1 by HW when failed device cannot be determined for RAS transactions in full ECC modes. This bit is usually set for uncorrectable error only, but error may be corrected by using PFD determined failed device to result in correctable error logging. Ignore for other ECC modes.

fields.name: X8_HALF_DEV_VALID
fields.description: Set to 1 by HW if failure identified is in half device only when 5x8 ECC is used. Valid only when error is correctable and retry_rd_err_log_address1.failed_dev_valid is set. Valid for 5x8 ECC only. RMemory Controller (MC) Registers-Diamond Rapids Processor

fields.name: POISON
fields.description: Set to 1 by HW if Poison value is read. This field is only valid with correctable error or no error cases on correction path.

fields.name: SDDC_DUE_S
fields.description: Set to 1 by HW for 10x4 SDDC 125b single device DUE. This bit is usually set for uncorrectable error only, but error may be corrected by using PFD determined failed device to result in correctable error logging. Ignore for other ECC modes.

fields.name: ADDDC_PC_BIT_FAILED
fields.description: ADDDC with column correction: set to 1 by HW if only PC bits has failed.

fields.name: ADDDC_FAILED_COL_IN_SPARE_DEV
fields.description: ADDDC with column correction: set to 1 by HW if half of the failed column is in the spare device.

fields.name: META_FAILED_COL_NUM
fields.description: this field logs the failed column number over the metadata+locator device. Bit 0 of this field is set when column 0 has failed (value 01), while bit 1 of this field is set when column 1 has failed (value 10). this field is only valid for ADDDC with column correction and when the column correction indication is set in the retry_rd_err_log register. This field is only valid with correctable error.

fields.name: DATA_FAILED_COL_NUM
fields.description: this field logs the failed column number over the data device. Data columns are numbered from 0 to 31. this field is only valid for ADDDC with column correction and when the column correction indication is set in the retry_rd_err_log register. This field is only valid with correctable error.

fields.name: SEFEEO
fields.description: System Error on Fatal Error Enable Overrid (SECEEO) This field controls the override of system errors generation in for fatal errors. When set to 1, it indicates that a System Error should be generated if a fatal error (ERR_FATAL) is reported by any of the RCiEPs associated with and including the RCEC regardless of the setting of the corresponding bit in the ROOTCTL register. When clear, the fatal errors are only propagated if the corresponding bit in ROOTCTL register is set.

fields.name: SENFEEO
fields.description: System Error on Non-Fatal Error Enable Override (SENFEEO) This field controls the override of system errors generation for non-fatal errors. When set to 1, it indicates that a System Error should be generated if a non-fatal error (ERR_NONFATAL) is reported by any of the RCiEPs associated with and including the RCEC regardless of the setting of the corresponding bit in the ROOTCTL register. When clear, the non-fatal errors are only propagated if the corresponding bit in ROOTCTL register is set.

fields.name: SECEEO
fields.description: System Error on Correctable Error Enable Override (SECEEO) This field controls override of system errors generation for correctable errors. When set to 1, it indicates that a System Error should be generated if a correctable error (ERR_COR) is reported by any of the RCiEPs associated with and including the RCEC regardless of the setting of the corresponding bit in the ROOTCTL register. When clear, the correctable errors are only propagated if the corresponding bit in ROOTCTL register is set.

fields.name: AEMN
fields.description: Advanced Error Interrupt Message Number (AEMN): This register indicates which MSI/MSI-X vector is used for the interrupt message generated in association with any of the status bits of this Capability. For MSI, the value in this register indicates the offset between the base Message Data and the interrupt message that is generated. Hardware is required to update this field so that it is correct if the number of MSI Messages assigned to the Function changes when software writes to the Multiple Message Enable field in the MSI Message Control register. For MSI-X, the value in this register indicates which MSI-X Table entry is used to generate the interrupt message. The entry must be one of the first 32 entries even if the Function implements more than 32 entries. For a given MSI-X implementation, the entry must remain constant. If both MSI and MSI-X are implemented, they are permitted to use different vectors, though software is permitted to enable only one mechanism at a time. If MSI-X is enabled, the value in this register must indicate the vector for MSI-X. If MSI is enabled or neither is enabled, the value in this register must indicate the vector for MSI. If software enables both MSI and MSI-X at the same time, the value in this register is undefined.

SCHEDULER_CA_SCRAMBLE.name: SCHEDULER_CA_SCRAMBLE
sections: Correctable error (UC=0, PCC=0) for data UC errors corrected by FM fill.

fields.name: SEED
fields.description: Initial seed for the scrambler LFSRs; default value is 0xFFFF

fields.name: EXTRA_GR8_CYCLE_ON_CMD
fields.description: This bit enables an extra scheduler pipe stage (HCLK, gear8 of DDR5 speed) on the cmd to dfi. It is required to be set (at boot time, before cmd scrambling would get enabled) in order to use the cmd parity error injection logic. And both copies of dfi_wrdata_timings need to be consistent. When set, the value of write_err_latency, and also pmmnt_ctrl0.err_latency, pdm_ctrl0.pmmnt_tpd, pdc_ctrl3.mrw_latency, are expected to be increased by 1 HCLK.

fields.name: TPHY_WRLATDATA
fields.description: Sum of tphy_wrlat and tphy_wrdata

fields.name: TPHY_WRCSLAT
fields.description: Specifies the number of DFI PHY clock cycles between when a write command is sent on the DFI command interface and when the associated dfi_wrdata_cs signal is asserted.

fields.name: TPHY_WRDATA
fields.description: Specifies the number of DFI PHY clock cycles from the time that the dfi_wrdata_en signal is asserted and when the associated write data is driven on the dfi_wrdata signal.

fields.name: TPHY_WRLAT
fields.description: Specifies the number of DFI PHY clock cycles allowed from the time that a write command is sent on the DFI command interface and when the dfi_wrdata_en signal is asserted.

fields.name: EN_RESET
fields.description: Enable scrambler reset after SRX without clock stop and after CA parity error

fields.name: EN_CRC
fields.description: CA CRC enable

fields.name: EN_SCRAMBLE
fields.description: CA scramble enable Diamond Rapids Processor Registers Specification June 2026 4666 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15

fields.name: SCRUB_EN
fields.description: Scrub enabled when set.

fields.name: STOP_ON_CMPL
fields.description: Stop patrol scrub at end of memory range. SMI is signaled by default when patrol scrub is completed and stopped.

fields.name: PTL_CMPL
fields.description: When stop_on_cmpl is enabled, patrol will stop at the end of the address range and set this bit. Patrol will resume from beginning of address range when this bit or stop_on_cmpl is cleared by SW and patrol scrub is still enabled by scrub_en.

fields.name: SCRUBISSUED
fields.description: When Set, the scrubaddress registers contain the last scrub address issued

fields.name: ISSUEONCE
fields.description: When Set, the patrol scrub engine will issue one patrol scrub and stop. The address in the scrubaddress registers is issued. Software is responsible to turn off periodic patrol before issuing patrol once (scrub_en should be set to 0). No cross product of patrol issue once with PkgC is allowed.

fields.name: STARTSCRUB
fields.description: When Set, the Patrol scrub engine will start from the address in the scrubaddress registers. Once the scrub is issued this bit is reset. To start patrol scrub from non-zero TAD, this bit should be set to 1 when scrub is enabled. The tad_rule field in scrubaddress register should be set to the value corresponding to address field when this bit is set.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved R Diamond Rapids Processor-Memory Controller (MC) Registers Registers Specification June 2026 4834 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 yu@

fields.name: DIS_PTRL_CMPL_SIG
fields.description: Set to 1 to disable signaling when patrol completed last channel address in continue scrubbing mode (does not disable signaling for stop_on_cmpl = 1 case).

fields.name: SCRUBINTERVAL
fields.description: Defines the interval in HCLKs between patrol scrub requests. The calculation for this register to get a scrub to every line in 24 hour is ((86400 seconds)/(memory capacity in Bytes/64))/(cycle time of HCLK in seconds). RESTRICTIONS: Can only be changed when patrol scrubs are disabled.

registers. Once the scrub is issued this bit is reset. To start patrol scrub from
non-zero TAD, this bit should be set to 1 when scrub is enabled. The tad_rule
field in scrubaddress register should be set to the value corresponding to address

SECSTS.name: SECSTS

fields.name: DPE
fields.description: This bit is set by the secondary side for a Type 1 Configuration Space header function whenever it receives a Poisoned TLP, regardless of the state in the Parity Error Response Enable (PERE) field of the Bridge Control Register (BCTL).

fields.name: RSE
fields.description: This bit is set by the secondary side for a Type 1 Configuration Space header function whenever it receives an ERR_FATAL or ERR_NONFATAL message.

fields.name: RMA
fields.description: This bit is set when the secondary side for Type 1 configuration space header function (for requests initiated by the Type 1 header function itself) receives a completion with Unsupported Requests Completion Status.

fields.name: RTA
fields.description: This bit is set when the secondary side for Type 1 Configuration Space Header Function (for Requests initiated by the Type 1 header Function itself) receives a completion with Completer About Completion Status.

fields.name: STA
fields.description: This bit is set when the secondary side for Type 1 configuration space header function (for requests completed by type 1 header functions itself) completes a Posted or Non-posted request as a Completer Abort error.

fields.name: DVT
fields.description: Not applicable to PCI Express. Hardwired to 0.

fields.name: MDPD
fields.description: This bit is set by the secondary side requester if the Parity Error Response Enable (PERE) bit in the Bridge Control Register (BCTL) is set and either of the following conditions occurs: Requester receives completion marked poisoned Requester sends a poisoned request (includes writes and messages) If the PERE bit in the Bridge Control Register (BCTL) is clear, this bit is never set.

SLOTCTL.name: SLOTCTL

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: IBPDD
fields.description: When Set, this bit disables the in-band presence detect mechanism from affecting the Presence Detect State bit, allowing that bit to report out-of-band presence detect exclusively. Otherwise, the Presence Detect State bit reflects the logical OR of the in-band and out-of-band presence detect mechanisms. In addition, the In-Band PD Disable bit governs the Component Presence state for the Downstream Component Presence field in the Link Status 2 Register. This bit must be implemented if the In-Band PD Disable Supported bit is 1b. Otherwise, this bit must be hardwired to 0b. Default value of this bit is 0b.

fields.name: /1S/V
fields.description: SCRE Field (SCRE): Writing a 1 to this field triggers an access (SCRT) to a eSPI-Device Config Register ('Go'). Note: eSPI Host clears this bit to 0 (& sets the SCRS field) when the transaction has completed on the eSPI bus. In the case of a configuration/status register read, the data is valid only after this bit has been cleared. Note: The SCRE is effective only if SCRS is clear.

fields.name: SCRS
fields.description: This field is set by upon the completion of a configuration register access (SCRE). Software must clear this field by writing all 1s before initiating another Device configuration register access (SCRE). No Response will be indicated as Fatal Error. LNKERR_SL*.Link Fatal Type 1 Cause can be used to identify if Fatal Error was No Response. • 0h: Status not valid R Diamond Rapids Processor-Secure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers Registers Specification June 2026 1690 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 • 2h: eSPI-Device Response CRC Error • 3h: eSPI-Device Response Fatal Error • 4h: eSPI-Device Response Non-Fatal Error • 5h - 6h: Reserved • 7h: No errors (transaction completed successfully)

fields.name: /1S
fields.description: SBLCL Field (SBLCL): When set, eSPI controller prevents writes (i.e., SET_CONFIGURATION) to any eSPI Specification defined eSPI-Device Capabilities and Configuration registers in the reserved register address range (0h - 7FFh). Access to eSPI-Device implementation specific configuration registers outside this range are not impacted by this lock bit and are always available - access protections to such registers are eSPI-Device implementation dependent. Note: This bit cannot be written to 0 once it has been set to 1. It can only be cleared by PLTRST# assertion. Note: This bit has no effect when PLTRST# is asserted. Implying this bit is reset on global reset. BIOS Note: BIOS must ensure that this bit is set to 1 after initial eSPI link configuration is over to prevent any further (unintentional or malicious) changes to the eSPI link configuration

fields.name: ESPINC
fields.description: • 00: eSPI interface is set to be enabled through (eSPI_INTERFACE_DIS = 0) soft strap AND it was detected (as in initial configuration cycles passed correctly) • 01: eSPI interface is set to be enabled through (eSPI_INTERFACE_DIS = 0) soft strap BUT it was NOT detected (as in initial configuration cycle failed) - the timer for this is also strapped through a softstrap (ESPI_DETECT_TIMER) • 10: RESERVED • 11: eSPI interface is disabled through soft strap (eSPI_INTERFACE_DIS = 1) Note that when EDAF mode is selected, eSPI interface soft strap is a don't care. Since sytem cannot boot without a working eSPI, this bit will never be set to '1 in EDAF mode.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: SID
fields.description: espi device ID (CS#) to which the eSPI-Device Configuration Register Access (SCRT) is directed • 00: espi device 0 (BMC) • 01: espi device 1 (when a second eSPI device is present) • 10 - 11: Reserved

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: SCRT
fields.description: • 00: eSPI-Device Configuration register read from address SCRA[11:0 (GET_CONFIG) • 01: eSPI-Device Configuration register write to address SCRA[11:0] (SET_CONFIG) • 10: eSPI-Device Status register read (GET_STATUS) • 11: In-Band Reset Note: Writes to eSPI-Device Configuration registers in the reserved address range (0h - 7FFh) are gated by the SBLCL bit. Note: Setting this field to 10 triggers a Get_Status command to the eSPI-Device. In this case, the SCRA field is ignored and only the lower 16-bits of the returned data (SLV_CFG_REG_DATA[15:0]) are valid. RSecure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers-Diamond Rapids Processor Note: Setting this field to 11 triggers an In-Band Reset command to the eSPI- Device. In this case, the SCRA field is ignored and no data is returned. This command resets the link for the targeted eSPI-Device to a default configuration. Software is responsible for reinitializing the link to optimized (higher performance) settings using these registers.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: SCRA
fields.description: Per eSPI Spec. / eSPI Compatibility Spec.

SMI_STS.name: SMI_STS
sections: When set, this indicates that the source of the interrupt or 1 Set bit 0

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: ESPI_VW_SMI_STS
fields.description: This bit is set if an eSPI agent is requesting an SMI#. This bit is set by the eSPI SMI request and cleared by BMC sending SMI deassertion VW. This bit is reset by PLTRST# assertion aka IA Warm reset.

fields.name: GPIO_UNLOCK_SMI_STS
fields.description: This bit will be set of the GPIO registers lockdown logic is requesting an SMI#. Writing a '1' to this bit position clears this bit to '0'. This bit is reset by PLTRST# assertion.

fields.name: SPI_SMI_STS
fields.description: This bit will be set when the SPI logic is requesting an SMI#. This bit is read only because the sticky status and enable bits associated with this function are located in the SPI registers.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: MONITOR_STS
fields.description: R Diamond Rapids Processor-Secure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers Registers Specification June 2026 1660 Intel Confidential Doc. No.: 793272, Rev.: 1.15 This bit will be set if the Trap/SMI logic has caused the SMI. This will occur when the CPU or a bus Driver accesses an assigned register (or a sequence of accesses).

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: SMBUS_SMI_STS
fields.description: This bit is sticky and is cleared by writing a 1 to this bit position. 1 = Indicates that the SMI# was caused by: 1. The SMBALERT# signal goes active and the SMB_SMI_EN bit is set and the SMBALERT_DIS bit is cleared, or 2. The SMBus responder/target receiving a HOST_NOTIFY message and the HOST_NOTIFY_INTREN and the SMB_SMI_EN bits are set. This bit is reset by PLTRST# assertion.

fields.name: ESPI_CTRL_SMI_STS
fields.description: 1 = Indicates the SMI# was caused by the eSPI Controller due to Error Conditions or BIOS WPD Related Events over eSPI. 0 = SMI# not caused by eSPI controller. NOTE: this bit is not sticky (as in reset by PLTRST# assertion). Writes to this bit will have no effect.

fields.name: PERIODIC_STS
fields.description: This bit will be set at the rate determined by the PER_SMI_SEL bits. If the PERIODIC_EN bit is also set, the integrated boot FW will generate an SMI#. This bit is cleared by writing a 1 to this bit position. This bit is reset by PLTRST# assertion.

fields.name: TCO_STS
fields.description: • 0 = SMI not caused by TCO logic. • 1 = Indicates SMI was caused by the TCO logic. NOTE: Will not cause wake event. This bit is cleared by writing a 1 to this bit position. This bit is reset by PLTRST# assertion.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: MCSMI_STS
fields.description: Software clears this bit by writing a 1 to it. • 0 = Indicates that there has been no access to the power management microcontroller range (62h or 66h). • 1 = Set if there has been an access to the power management microcontroller range (62h or 66h) and the Microcontroller Decode Enable #1 bit in the LPC Bridge I/O Enables configuration register is 1 (D31:F0:Offset 82h:bit 11). If this bit is set, and the MCSMI_EN bit is also set, the S3M IBL will generate an SMI#. This bit is reset by PLTRST# assertion.

fields.name: GPIO_SMI_STS
fields.description: This bit will be a 1 if any GPIO that is enabled to trigger SMI is asserted. GPIOs that are not routed to cause an SMI will have no effect on this bit. This bit is NOT sticky (reset by PLTRST assertion). Writes to this bit will have no effect. Note: See the GPIO chapter for the individual GPIO SMI status, enable, and routing bit definitions.

fields.name: GPE0_STS
fields.description: RSecure Startup Services Module (S3M) Registers-Diamond Rapids Processor There are several status/enable bit pairs in GPE0_STS/EN_127_96 that are capable of triggering SMI#s. This bit is a logical OR of all of those pairs (i.e. this bit is asserted whenever at least one of those pairs has both the status and enable bit asserted). This bit is NOT sticky. Writes to this bit will have no effect. Note: The setting of this bit does not cause the SMI#. The following bit pairs are included in this logical OR: - GPE0_STS/EN_127_96 [20, 11, 2]

fields.name: PM1_STS_REG
fields.description: This is an OR of the bits (except for bits 5 and 4) in the ACPI PM1 Status Reg. Not sticky. Writes to this bit have no effect. Note: The setting of this bit does not cause the SMI#.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: SWSMI_TMR_STS
fields.description: This bit will be set to 1 by the hardware when the Software SMI# Timer expires. This bit will remain 1 until the software writes a 1 to this bit. This bit is reset by PLTRST# assertion.

fields.name: APM_STS
fields.description: SMI# was generated by a write access to the APM control register and if the APMC_EN bit is set. This bit is cleared by writing a one to its bit position. This bit is reset by PLTRST# assertion.

fields.name: SMI_ON_SLP_EN_STS
fields.description: This bit will be set by the integrated boot FW when a write access attempts to set the SLP_EN bit. This bit is cleared by writing a 1 to this bit position. This bit is reset by PLTRST# assertion.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: BIOS_STS
fields.description: This bit gets set by hardware when a 1 is written by software to the GBL_RLS bit. When both BIOS_EN and the BIOS_STS bit are set, an SMI# will be generated. The BIOS_STS bit is cleared when software writes a 1 to this bit position. This bit is reset by PLTRST# assertion.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved

fields.name: SMB_MC_SMI_STS
fields.description: This bit will be a 1 if SMB_MC trigger SMI is asserted. This bit is NOT sticky. Writes to this bit will have no effect.

fields.name: REGION_SIZE
fields.description: This field selects the granularity for the sparing copy operation: 00=Bank 01=Rank 1X=Reserved

fields.name: ADDDC_SPARING
fields.description: This bit causes the sparing copy to be ADDDC sparing when sparing copy has been started via the spare_enable bit. This register is locked by the DISABLE_ADDDC_SPARING bit from IMC_FUSE_DOWNLOAD register.

fields.name: REVERSE_SPARE
fields.description: Setting this bit will cause sparing engine to be run in reverse (e.g., move from virtual lockstep back to independent) when sparing has been started via the spare_enable bit. Example usage cases are upgrading a region failure from bank to rank, or unpair existing ADDDC pair to repair with different rank/bank, or testing.

fields.name: ENABLE_SPARE
fields.description: Enable ADDDC sparing copy when set to 1. Hardware clears this bit after the sparing completion.

SPPR_CTRL2.name: SPPR_CTRL2
sections: Correctable error (UC=0, PCC=0) for data UC errors corrected by FM fill.

fields.name: CREDITS_MEM_INIT
fields.description: This is the total number of write transactions that the memory scrub engine can have outstanding to initialize memory outside of BIOS memory during meminit Phase 1. This value must be programmed to a portion of the total writes that can be handled by the scheduler. The remaining write credits available in the scheduler will be made available to BIOS traffic as it accesses BIOS memory region. The value in this field is used to control partitioning of the write bandwidth between BIOS traffic and initialization of non-BIOS memory. The higher the value in this field, the faster the non-BIOS memory is initialized but write bandwidth of non-BIOS traffic is impacted.

fields.name: NUM_LOOPS
fields.description: Number of loops the sPPR H/W engine performs copy and PPR sequences. Only value of 1 is supported.

fields.name: COPY_CL_SIZE
fields.description: Number of cache lines copies by sPPR H/W per loop. The number of loops (X) depends on DRAM page size and MC IP WDB size. For example, 16Gb x4 DRAM has 1KB page. Each row contains (1KB/DRAM X 8DRAM's)/64B = 128 cache lines per sub-channel. 16Gb x8 DIMM has 64 cache lines per sub-channel. MC WDB size is more than 128 cache lines. This means that the loop number X=1 in both cases, and copy_cl_size is 128 for 16Gb x4 DIMM and 64 for 16Gb x8 DIMM.

fields.name: FAST_MEMINIT_EN
fields.description: Writing 1 to fast_meminit_en will enable fast mode for MemInit engine. This can only be used with Phase0-only application of MemInit. This must be set when meminit_en is set to 1 if this mode is used.

fields.name: EN_INTRPT_ON_CMPL
fields.description: Set to 1 to enable interrupt signaling on completion of MemInit phase 1. Interrupt type is selected via smisparectl

fields.name: MEMINIT_START
fields.description: Transition from 0->1 start MemInit engine. HW reset the bit to 0 after MemInit starts.

fields.name: MEMINIT_EN
fields.description: Writing 1 to meminit_en will enable the MemInit engine. BIOS disable memInit engine at end of meminit phase 1

fields.description: If FREEZELBE is set, then this field decides the width at which lane trimming will be automatically disabled (by freezing the LBE logic). 00: x1 01: x2 10: x4 (default) 11: x8

fields.name: FREEZELBE
fields.description: If set, when UXI Width Degrade trims off lanes, freeze the state of the LBE (clear the LBE enable and leave error counts at values used for trim). This is in addition to the LBECTL2.FREEZEMODE setting.

fields.name: IORECALREQRSTLBE
fields.description: If set, after UXI Width Degrade logic initiates an IO Recal, it clears the error counts of the LBE

fields.name: IORECALSUCCTO
fields.description: Timeout value for the UXI Width Degrade IORECAL_DONE state. This timer indicates the amount of time an IORECAL applies to the LBE trigger for lane trimming. Prior to this timer expiring, the most recent IORECAL would qualify as a pre-lane trim IORECAL. After this timer expires, a new IORECAL must be done prior to trimming lanes. If IORECAL is not enabled for UXI PAM4, then this timer is not used. This timer should only count while the link is in data stream (L0 or Rec/Cfg.Idle) [9:8] Unit 0: 1ms 1: 16ms

fields.name: VIRAL_STATE
fields.description: Indicates that the IP is in a viral state. When set, all inbound and outbound requests are aborted. If software writes a 1, the IP exits the viral state. This state bit is cleared by warm reset. Formerly known as iio_viral_state.

fields.name: /P
fields.description: Sticky Viral Status (VIRAL_STATUS): Indicates that a prior viral event occurred. This bit has no effect on hardware and does not indicate that the IP is currently in the viral state. This bit is persistent through warm reset (sticky), even though the viral state is not. Formerly known as iio_viral_status.

VWERR_SLV1.eds_description: This register is used to control error reporting for the eSPI Virtual Wire Channel for the second eSPI device. Note: Accesses to this register must respond with a U/R when a second eSPI device is not present (i.e., in a single Device configuration). The register definition is identical to that of VWERR_SLV0, with the following exception: VWNSMIEL, VWNMIOE, VWSMIOE (bits [28:26]): These bits are not supported. The corresponding bits for Device0 in VWERR_SLV0 register cover NMI# and SMI# transmission to both Devices.
